## Create an email template

<a id="opIdPOST_Create_Email_Template"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/notifications/email-templates \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "active": true,
    "bccEmailAddress": "user@example.com",
    "ccEmailAddress": "user@example.com",
    "ccEmailType": "SpecificEmails",
    "description": "Email when an account is edited",
    "emailBody": "Dear user,<p>the account <Account.Name> has been edited. <p>Example Co. Ltd.",
    "emailSubject": "Account <Account.Number> has been edited",
    "encodingType": "UTF8",
    "eventTypeName": "AccountEdit",
    "fromEmailAddress": null,
    "fromEmailType": "TenantEmail",
    "fromName": "Example Co. Ltd.",
    "isHtml": true,
    "name": "Account Edit Email",
    "replyToEmailAddress": null,
    "replyToEmailType": "TenantEmail",
    "toEmailAddress": null,
    "toEmailType": "BillToContact"
  }'
```

`POST /notifications/email-templates`

Creates an email template.

**Note**: This operation is only applicable to email templates for custom events.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "bccEmailAddress": "user@example.com",
  "ccEmailAddress": "user@example.com",
  "ccEmailType": "SpecificEmails",
  "description": "Email when an account is edited",
  "emailBody": "Dear user,<p>the account <Account.Name> has been edited. <p>Example Co. Ltd.",
  "emailSubject": "Account <Account.Number> has been edited",
  "encodingType": "UTF8",
  "eventTypeName": "AccountEdit",
  "fromEmailAddress": null,
  "fromEmailType": "TenantEmail",
  "fromName": "Example Co. Ltd.",
  "isHtml": true,
  "name": "Account Edit Email",
  "replyToEmailAddress": null,
  "replyToEmailType": "TenantEmail",
  "toEmailAddress": null,
  "toEmailType": "BillToContact"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-email-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Authorization|header|string|true|`Bearer {token}` for a valid OAuth token.<br><br>Note that you must regenerate the OAuth token after the Custom Events feature is enabled in your Zuora tenant. The OAuth tokens generated before this feature is turned on will not work.<br>|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|body|body|[POSTPublicEmailTemplateRequest](#schemapostpublicemailtemplaterequest)|true|The request body to create an email template.|
|» active|body|boolean|false|The status of the email template. The default value is true.|
|» bccEmailAddress|body|string(email)|false|The email bcc address.|
|» ccEmailAddress|body|string|false|The email CC address.|
|» ccEmailType|body|string|false|Email CC type:<br>* When EventType is CDC/External and 'ReferenceObjectType' in EventType is associated to Account, ccEmailType can be ALL values in enum. <br>* When EventType is CDC/External and 'ReferenceObjectType' in EventType is not associated to Account, ccEmailType MUST be TenantAdmin, RunOwner or SpecificEmail. <br>* When EventType is CDC/External and 'ReferenceObjectType' in EventType is EMPTY, ccEmailType MUST be TenantAdmin, RunOwner or SpecificEmail.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the email template.|
|» emailBody|body|string|true|The email body. You can add merge fields in the email object using angle brackets. <br>You can also embed HTML tags if 'isHtml' is true.|
|» emailSubject|body|string|true|The email subject. Users can add merge fields in the email subject using angle brackets.|
|» encodingType|body|string|false|The endcode type of the email body.|
|» eventTypeName|body|string|true|The name of the event type. <br>|
|» eventTypeNamespace|body|string|false|The namespace of the `eventTypeName` field. The `eventTypeName` has the `user.notification` namespace by default. <br><br>Note that if the `eventTypeName` is a standard event type, you must specify the `com.zuora.notification` namespace; otherwise, you will get an error.<br><br>For example, if you want to create an email template on the `OrderActionProcessed` event, you must specify `com.zuora.notification` for this field.         <br>|
|» fromEmailAddress|body|string|false|If fromEmailType is SpecificEmail, this field is required.|
|» fromEmailType|body|string|true|The type of the email.|
|» fromName|body|string|false|The name of the email sender.|
|» isHtml|body|boolean|false|Specifies whether the style of email body is HTML. The default value is false.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the email template, a unique name in a tenant.|
|» replyToEmailAddress|body|string|false|If replyToEmailType is SpecificEmail, this field is required.|
|» replyToEmailType|body|string|false|Type of the replyTo email.|
|» toEmailAddress|body|string|false|If toEmailType is SpecificEmail, this field is required.|
|» toEmailType|body|string|true|Email receive type.<br>* When EventType is CDC/External and 'ReferenceObjectType' in EventType is associated to Account, toEmailType can be ALL values in enum. <br>* When EventType is CDC/External and 'ReferenceObjectType' in EventType is not associated to Account, toEmailType MUST be TenantAdmin, RunOwner or SpecificEmail.<br>* When EventType is CDC/External and 'ReferenceObjectType' in EventType is EMPTY, toEmailType MUST be TenantAdmin, RunOwner or SpecificEmail.|

|» fromEmailType|TenantEmail|

## Update an email template

<a id="opIdPUT_Update_Email_Template"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/notifications/email-templates/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "active": true,
    "bccEmailAddress": "user@example.com",
    "ccEmailAddress": "user@example.com",
    "ccEmailType": "SpecificEmails",
    "description": "Email when an account is edited",
    "emailBody": "Dear user,<p>the account <Account.Name> has been edited. <p>Example Co. Ltd.",
    "emailSubject": "Account <Account.Number> has been edited",
    "encodingType": "UTF8",
    "fromEmailAddress": null,
    "fromEmailType": "TenantEmail",
    "fromName": "Example Co. Ltd.",
    "isHtml": true,
    "name": "Account Edit Email",
    "replyToEmailAddress": null,
    "replyToEmailType": "TenantEmail",
    "toEmailAddress": null,
    "toEmailType": "BillToContact"
  }'
```

`PUT /notifications/email-templates/{id}`

Updates an email template.

**Note**: This operation is only applicable to email templates for custom events.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "bccEmailAddress": "user@example.com",
  "ccEmailAddress": "user@example.com",
  "ccEmailType": "SpecificEmails",
  "description": "Email when an account is edited",
  "emailBody": "Dear user,<p>the account <Account.Name> has been edited. <p>Example Co. Ltd.",
  "emailSubject": "Account <Account.Number> has been edited",
  "encodingType": "UTF8",
  "fromEmailAddress": null,
  "fromEmailType": "TenantEmail",
  "fromName": "Example Co. Ltd.",
  "isHtml": true,
  "name": "Account Edit Email",
  "replyToEmailAddress": null,
  "replyToEmailType": "TenantEmail",
  "toEmailAddress": null,
  "toEmailType": "BillToContact"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-email-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Authorization|header|string|true|`Bearer {token}` for a valid OAuth token.<br><br>Note that you must regenerate the OAuth token after the Custom Events feature is enabled in your Zuora tenant. The OAuth tokens generated before this feature is turned on will not work.<br>|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the email template to be updated.|
|body|body|[PUTPublicEmailTemplateRequest](#schemaputpublicemailtemplaterequest)|true|The request body to update an email template.|
|» active|body|boolean|false|The status of the email template.|
|» bccEmailAddress|body|string(email)|false|Email bcc address.|
|» ccEmailAddress|body|string|false|Email cc address.|
|» ccEmailType|body|string|false|Email cc type.<br>* When EventType is CDC/External and 'ReferenceObjectType' in EventType is associated to Account, ccEmailType can be ALL values in enum. <br>* When EventType is CDC/External and 'ReferenceObjectType' in EventType is not associated to Account, ccEmailType MUST be TenantAdmin, RunOwner or SpecificEmail.<br>* When EventType is CDC/External and 'ReferenceObjectType' in EventType is EMPTY, ccEmailType MUST be TenantAdmin, RunOwner or SpecificEmail.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the email template.|
|» emailBody|body|string|false|The email body. You can add merge fields in the email object using angle brackets. <br>User can also embed html tags if 'isHtml' is true.|
|» emailSubject|body|string|false|The email subject. You can add merge fields in the email subject using angle brackets.|
|» encodingType|body|string|false|The endcode type of the email body.|
|» fromEmailAddress|body|string|false|If fromEmailType is SpecificEmail, this field is required|
|» fromEmailType|body|string|false|The type of fromEmail.|
|» fromName|body|string|false|The name of email sender.|
|» isHtml|body|boolean|false|Specifies whether the style of email body is HTML.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the email template.|
|» replyToEmailAddress|body|string|false|If replyToEmailType is SpecificEmail, this field is required.|
|» replyToEmailType|body|string|false|The type of the reply email.|
|» toEmailAddress|body|string|false|If toEmailType is SpecificEmail, this field is required.|
|» toEmailType|body|string|false|Email receive type.<br>* When EventType is CDC/External and 'ReferenceObjectType' in EventType is associated to Account, toEmailType can be ALL values in enum. <br>* When EventType is CDC/External and 'ReferenceObjectType' in EventType is not associated to Account, toEmailType MUST be TenantAdmin, RunOwner or SpecificEmail. <br>* When EventType is CDC/External and 'ReferenceObjectType' in EventType is EMPTY, toEmailType MUST be TenantAdmin, RunOwner or SpecificEmail.|

## Create a notification definition

<a id="opIdPOST_Create_Notification_Definition"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/notifications/notification-definitions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "active": true,
    "callout": {
      "active": true,
      "calloutAuth": {
        "domain": "example_domain",
        "password": "example_password",
        "preemptive": true,
        "username": "example_user"
      },
      "calloutBaseurl": "https://www.example.com/callout/AccountEdit",
      "calloutParams": {
        "AccountName": "<Account.Name>",
        "AccountNumber": "<Account.AccountNumber>"
      },
      "calloutRetry": true,
      "description": "Callout when an account is edited",
      "eventTypeName": "AccountEdit",
      "httpMethod": "POST",
      "name": "Callout for Account Edited",
      "requiredAuth": true
    },
    "calloutActive": true,
    "communicationProfileId": "6e569e1e05f040eda51a927b140c0ac5",
    "description": "Notification sent out when an account is edited",
    "emailActive": true,
    "emailTemplateId": "6e569e1e05f040eda51a927b140c0ac6",
    "eventTypeName": "AccountEdit",
    "filterRule": {
      "condition": "Account.Balance >= _VIP_BALANCE_AMOUNT && Account.Status == _ACCOUNT_STATUS",
      "description": "Filter rule to test if an account is a VIP account",
      "parameters": {
        "_ACCOUNT_STATUS": {
          "description": "The status of the VIP Account",
          "displayName": "VIP Account Status",
          "options": [
            "Draft",
            "Active",
            "Canceled"
          ],
          "valueType": "STRING"
        },
        "_VIP_BALANCE_AMOUNT": {
          "description": "The minimum account balance",
          "displayName": "VIP Account Balance",
          "options": null,
          "valueType": "BIG_DECIMAL"
        }
      }
    },
    "filterRuleParams": {
      "_EDITED_FROM": "UI",
      "_VIP_ACCOUNT_BALANCE": "100000"
    },
    "name": "Account Edit Notification"
  }'
```

`POST /notifications/notification-definitions`

Creates a notification definition. If a filter rule is specified, it will be evaluated to
see if the notification definition is qualified to handle the incoming events 
during runtime. If the notification is qualified, it will send the email and
invoke the callout if it has an email template or a callout. See a step-by-step guide for
[creating a custom notification](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-guides/#Callout-to-external-system-for-provisioning-or-entitlements)
in [Zuora API Guides](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-guides/).

**Note**: This operation is only applicable to notifications for custom events.

<h3 id="create-a-notification-definition-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Authorization|header|string|true|`Bearer {token}` for a valid OAuth token.<br><br>Note that you must regenerate the OAuth token after the Custom Events feature is enabled in your Zuora tenant. The OAuth tokens generated before this feature is turned on will not work.<br>|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|body|body|[POSTPublicNotificationDefinitionRequest](#schemapostpublicnotificationdefinitionrequest)|true|The request body used to create the notification definition.|
|» active|body|boolean|false|The status of the notification definition. The default value is true.|
|» callout|body|object|false|none|
|» » active|body|boolean|false|The status of the callout. The default is true.|
|» » calloutAuth|body|[CalloutAuth](#schemacalloutauth)|false|If requiredAuth is true, this object is required.|
|» » calloutBaseurl|body|string(url)|true|The callout URL. It must start with 'https://'|
|» » calloutParams|body|[CalloutMergeFields](#schemacalloutmergefields)|false|A key-value map of merge fields of this callout.<br>|
|» » calloutRetry|body|boolean|false|Specified whether to retry the callout when the callout fails. The default is true.|
|» » description|body|string|false|Description for the callout.|
|» » eventTypeName|body|string|true|The name of the event type.|
|» » httpMethod|body|string|true|The HTTP method of the callout.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the created callout.|
|» » requiredAuth|body|boolean|true|Specifies whether the callout requires auth.|
|» calloutActive|body|boolean|false|The status of the callout action. Default value is false.|
|» communicationProfileId|body|string|false|The profile that notification definition belongs to. <br><br>You can use the [Query Action](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/Action_POSTquery) to get the communication profile Id. See the following request sample:<br><br>`{<br>    "queryString": "select Id, ProfileName from CommunicationProfile"<br> }`<br><br>If you do not pass the communicationProfileId, notification service will be automatically added to the 'Default Profile'.<br>|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the notification definition.|
|» emailActive|body|boolean|false|The status of the email action. The default value is false.|
|» emailTemplateId|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of the email template. If emailActive is true, an email template is required. And EventType of the email template MUST be the same as the eventType.|
|» eventTypeName|body|string|true|The name of the event type. <br>|
|» eventTypeNamespace|body|string|false|The namespace of the `eventTypeName` field. The `eventTypeName` has the `user.notification` namespace by default. <br>          <br>For example, if you want to create a notification definition on the `OrderActionProcessed` event, you must specify `com.zuora.notification` for this field.<br>|
|» filterRule|body|object|false|none|
|» » condition|body|string|true|The filter rule conditions, written in [JEXL](http://commons.apache.org/proper/commons-jexl/).<br>The rule might contain event context merge fields and data source merge fields. Data source merge fields must be from [the base object of the event or from the joined objects of the base object](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/DC_Developers/M_Export_ZOQL#Data_Sources_and_Objects). Notifications with invalid merge fields will fail to evaluate, thus will not be invoked. For example, to filter an invoice posted notification to only invoices with an amount over 1000, you would define the following condition:<br><br>```Invoice.Amount > 1000```<br><br>There are conventions and keywords you need to be aware of. For example:<br><br>* `Invoice.Amount` refers to the `Amount` field of the Zuora object `Invoice`.<br><br>* Unlike Event Triggers, there is no access to variables with the `_old` suffix. Fields with the `_old` suffix are only available on Event Trigger conditions.<br>|
|» » description|body|string|false|The description of the filter rule.|
|» » parameters|body|[FilterRuleParameterDefinitions](#schemafilterruleparameterdefinitions)|true|The parameters of the filter rule and their name must match those in the filter rule. And all parameters must be defined in the event type payload. The name of parameters can't be duplicate. The following reserved keywords should not be used as a parameter name: `AttachmentList`, `RecipientList`, `RecipientType`, `Exceptions`, `OCP_OBJECT_TYPE`, `OCP_OBJECT_ID`, `OCP_TRIGGER_BY`<br>|
|» filterRuleParams|body|[FilterRuleParameterValues](#schemafilterruleparametervalues)|false|The parameter values used to configure the filter rule.<br>|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the notification definition, unique per communication profile.|

|» » active|body|boolean|false|The status of the callout. The default is true.|
|» » calloutAuth|body|[CalloutAuth](#schemacalloutauth)|false|If requiredAuth is true, this object is required.|
|» » calloutBaseurl|body|string(url)|true|The callout URL. It must start with 'https://'|

|» » httpMethod|body|string|true|The HTTP method of the callout.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the created callout.|
|» » requiredAuth|body|boolean|true|Specifies whether the callout requires auth.|
|» calloutActive|body|boolean|false|The status of the callout action. The default value is false.|
|» communicationProfileId|body|string(uuid)|false|The profile that notification definition belongs to. If you want to<br>update the notification to a system notification, you should pass<br>'SystemNotification'. '<br><br>* When EventType is CDC/External and 'ReferenceObjectType' in EventType is associated to Account, comunicationProfileId can be 'SystemNotification'/Empty/UUID. <br><br>* When EventType is CDC/External and 'ReferenceObjectType' in EventType is not  associated to Account, comunicationProfileId can be 'SystemNotification'/Empty. <br><br>* When EventType is CDC/External and 'ReferenceObjectType' in EventType is EMPTY, comunicationProfileId can be 'SystemNotification'/Empty.<br>|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the notification definition.|
|» emailActive|body|boolean|false|The status of the email action. The default is false.|
|» emailTemplateId|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of the email template. If emailActive is updated from<br>false to true, an email template is required, and the EventType of<br>the email template MUST be the same as the EventType of the notification definition.<br>|
|» filterRule|body|object|false|none|
|» » condition|body|string|true|The filter rule conditions, written in [JEXL](http://commons.apache.org/proper/commons-jexl/).<br>The rule might contain event context merge fields and data source merge fields. Data source merge fields must be from [the base object of the event or from the joined objects of the base object](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/DC_Developers/M_Export_ZOQL#Data_Sources_and_Objects). Notifications with invalid merge fields will fail to evaluate, thus will not be invoked. For example, to trigger an event when an invoice is posted with the amount over 1000, you would define the following condition on the `Invoice` object:<br><br>```changeType == 'UPDATE' && Invoice.Status == 'Posted' && Invoice.Status_old != 'Posted' && Invoice.Amount > 1000```<br><br>There are conventions and keywords you need to be aware of. For example:<br><br>* `changeType` is a keyword to specify what kind of change happened to the object. Allowed values are `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`.<br><br>* `Invoice.Status` refers to field `Status` of the Zuora object `Invoice`.<br><br>* A variable with the `_old` suffix means it’s a previous value of the corresponding object field. The "_old" fields are only available on the base objects.<br>|
|» » description|body|string|false|The description of the filter rule.|
|» » parameters|body|[FilterRuleParameterDefinitions](#schemafilterruleparameterdefinitions)|true|The parameters of the filter rule and their name must match those in the filter rule. And all parameters must be defined in the event type payload. The name of parameters can't be duplicate. The following reserved keywords should not be used as a parameter name: `AttachmentList`, `RecipientList`, `RecipientType`, `Exceptions`, `OCP_OBJECT_TYPE`, `OCP_OBJECT_ID`, `OCP_TRIGGER_BY`<br>|
|» filterRuleParams|body|[FilterRuleParameterValues](#schemafilterruleparametervalues)|false|The parameter values used to configure the filter rule.<br>|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the notification definition, which is unique in the profile.|

## Delete a notification definition

<a id="opIdDELETE_Delete_Notification_Definition"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/notifications/notification-definitions/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /notifications/notification-definitions/{id}`

Deletes a notification definition.

**Note**: This operation is only applicable to notifications for custom events.


<h3 id="delete-a-notification-definition-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Authorization|header|string|true|`Bearer {token}` for a valid OAuth token.<br><br>Note that you must regenerate the OAuth token after the Custom Events feature is enabled in your Zuora tenant. The OAuth tokens generated before this feature is turned on will not work.<br>|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|id|path|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the notification definition to be deleted.|


## List callout notification histories

<a id="opIdGET_CalloutHistory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/notification-history/callout \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v1/notification-history/callout`

Describes how to get a notification history for callouts.


<h3 id="list-callout-notification-histories-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|pageSize|query|integer|false|Number of rows returned per page.<br>|
|endTime|query|string(date-time)|false|The final date and time of records to be returned. Defaults to now. Use format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.|
|startTime|query|string(date-time)|false|The initial date and time of records to be returned. Defaults to (end time - 1 day). Use format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.|
|objectId|query|string|false|The ID of an object that triggered a callout notification. <br><br>**Note**: If the `objectId` is present in query parameters, the `eventCategory` will be ignored and the `failedOnly` will be treated as `false`.<br>|
|failedOnly|query|boolean|false|If `true`, only return failed records. If `false`, return all records in the given date range. The default value is `true`.<br><br>**Note**: The `failedOnly` will be treated as `false` if the `objectId` is present in query parameters.<br>|
|eventCategory|query|string|false|Category of records to be returned by event category.<br><br>The following formats are supported:<br>* `{Event Type Namespace}:{Event Type Name}` if the Custom Events feature is enabled in your tenant. For example: `user.notification:NewSubscriptionCreated`.<br>* Numeric code of the event category if the Custom Events feature is not enabled in your tenant. For example, `1210`. See [Event Category Code](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/DC_Developers/AA_REST_API/Event_Categories_for_Notification_Histories) for more information.<br><br>**Note**: The `eventCategory` will be ignored if the `objectId` is present in query parameters.<br>|
|includeResponseContent|query|boolean|false|none|

## List email notification histories

<a id="opIdGET_EmailHistory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/notification-history/email \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v1/notification-history/email`

Describes how to get a notification history for notification emails.


## Notes
Request parameters and their values may be appended with a "?" following the HTTPS GET request.  Additional request parameter are separated by "&". 

For example:

`GET https://rest.zuora.com/v1/notification-history/email?startTime=2015-01-12T00:00:00&endTime=2015-01-15T00:00:00&failedOnly=false&eventCategory=1000&pageSize=1`


<h3 id="list-email-notification-histories-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|pageSize|query|integer|false|Number of rows returned per page.<br>|
|endTime|query|string(date-time)|false|The end date and time of records to be returned. Defaults to now. Use format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss. The maximum date range (endTime - startTime) is three days.|
|startTime|query|string(date-time)|false|The initial date and time of records to be returned. Defaults to (end time - 1 day). Use format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss. The maximum date range (endTime - startTime) is three days.|
|objectId|query|string|false|The Id of an object that triggered an email notification.<br><br>**Note**: If the `objectId` is present in query parameters, the `eventCategory` will be ignored and the `failedOnly` will be treated as `false`.<br>|

<h1 id="api-reference-billing-oauth">OAuth</h1>

## Create an OAuth token

<a id="opIdcreateToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/oauth/token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'client_id=stringstringstringstringstringstring&client_secret=string&grant_type=client_credentials'
```

`POST /oauth/token`

Creates a bearer token that enables an OAuth client to authenticate with the Zuora REST API. The OAuth client must have been created using the Zuora UI. See [Authentication](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#section/Authentication) for more information.

**Note:** When using this operation, do not set any authentication headers such as `Authorization`, `apiAccessKeyId`, or `apiSecretAccessKey`.

You should not use this operation to generate a large number of bearer tokens in a short period of time; each token should be used until it expires. If you receive a 429 Too Many Requests response when using this operation, reduce the frequency of requests. This endpoint is rate limited by IP address. The rate limit is 100 requests per minute.


> Body parameter

```yaml
client_id: stringstringstringstringstringstring
client_secret: string
grant_type: client_credentials
```

<h3 id="create-an-oauth-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» client_id|body|string|true|The Client ID of the OAuth client.<br>|
|» client_secret|body|string|true|The Client Secret that was displayed when the OAuth client was created.<br>|
|» grant_type|body|string|true|The OAuth grant type that will be used to generate the token. The value of this parameter must be `client_credentials`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» grant_type|client_credentials|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "access_token": "c652cbc0ea384b9f81856a93a2a74538",
  "expires_in": 3599,
  "jti": "c652cbc0ea384b9f81856a93a2a74539",
  "scope": "user.7c4d5433dc234c369a01b9719ecd059f entity.1a2b7a37-3e7d-4cb3-b0e2-883de9e766cc entity.c92ed977-510c-4c48-9b51-8d5e848671e9 service.echo.read tenant.19",
  "token_type": "bearer"
}
```

<h1 id="api-reference-billing-operations">Operations</h1>

## Generate a billing preview

<a id="opIdPOST_BillingPreview"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/operations/billing-preview \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "accountId": "402890b75972406c0159724cd4d00011",
    "assumeRenewal": "None",
    "chargeTypeToExclude": "",
    "includingEvergreenSubscription": "true",
    "targetDate": "2017-05-10"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/operations/billing-preview`

**Note:** The Billing Preview feature is in **Limited Availability**. If you wish to have access to the feature, submit a request at [Zuora Global Support](http://support.zuora.com/). 


Generates a preview of future invoice items for one customer account. Use the BillingPreview call to calculate how much a single customer will be invoiced from the most recent invoice to a specific end of term date in the future.

Additionally, you can use the BillingPreview service to access real-time data on an individual customer's usage consumption. 

The BillingPreview call does not calculate taxes for charges in the subscription.

If you have the Invoice Settlement feature enabled, you can also generate a preview of future credit memo items for one customer account. The Invoice Settlement feature is generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 296 (March 2021). This feature includes Unapplied Payments, Credit and Debit Memo, and Invoice Item Settlement. If you want to enable Invoice Settlement, see [Invoice Settlement Enablement and Checklist Guide](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement/Invoice_Settlement_Migration_Checklist_and_Guide) for more information. 


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "accountId": "402890b75972406c0159724cd4d00011",
  "assumeRenewal": "None",
  "chargeTypeToExclude": "",
  "includingEvergreenSubscription": "true",
  "targetDate": "2017-05-10"
}
```

<h3 id="generate-a-billing-preview-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|body|body|[PostBillingPreviewParam](#schemapostbillingpreviewparam)|true|none|
|» accountId|body|string|true|ID of the customer account to which the billing preview applies.<br>|
|» assumeRenewal|body|string|false|Indicates whether to generate a preview of future invoice items and credit memo items with the assumption that the subscriptions are renewed.<br><br>Set one of the following values in this field to decide how the assumption is applied in the billing preview.<br><br>  * **All:** The assumption is applied to all the subscriptions. Zuora generates preview invoice item data and credit memo item data from the first day of the customer's next billing period to the target date.<br>  <br>  * **None:** (Default) The assumption is not applied to the subscriptions. Zuora generates preview invoice item data and credit memo item data based on the current term end date and the target date.<br>  <br>    * If the target date is later than the current term end date, Zuora generates preview invoice item data and credit memo item data from the first day of the customer's next billing period to the current term end date.<br><br>    * If the target date is earlier than the current term end date, Zuora generates preview invoice item data and credit memo item data from the first day of the customer's next billing period to the target date.<br><br>  * **Autorenew:** The assumption is applied to the subscriptions that have auto-renew enabled. Zuora generates preview invoice item data and credit memo item data from the first day of the customer's next billing period to the target date.<br><br>**Note:** <br>  - This field can only be used if the subscription renewal term is not set to 0.  <br>  <br>  <br>  - The credit memo item data is only available if you have Invoice Settlement feature enabled. The Invoice Settlement feature is generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 296 (March 2021). This feature includes Unapplied Payments, Credit and Debit Memo, and Invoice Item Settlement. If you want to enable Invoice Settlement, see [Invoice Settlement Enablement and Checklist Guide](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement/Invoice_Settlement_Migration_Checklist_and_Guide) for more information.<br>|
|» chargeTypeToExclude|body|string|false|The charge types to exclude from the billing preview.<br><br>**Possible values:** OneTime, Recurring, Usage, and any combination of these values.<br>|
|» includingEvergreenSubscription|body|boolean|false|Indicates if evergreen subscriptions are included in the billingPreview call.<br>|
|» targetDate|body|string(date)|true|The target date for the billingPreview call. The billingPreview call generates preview invoice item data and credit memo item data from the first day of the customer's next billing period to the TargetDate. <br><br>If the TargetDate is later than the subscription current term end date, the preview invoice item data and credit memo item data is generated from the first day of the customer's next billing period to the current term end date. If you want to generate preview invoice item data and credit memo item data past the end of the subscription current term, specify the `AssumeRenewal` field in the request.<br><br><br>**Note:** The credit memo item data is only available if you have Invoice Settlement feature enabled. The Invoice Settlement feature is generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 296 (March 2021). This feature includes Unapplied Payments, Credit and Debit Memo, and Invoice Item Settlement. If you want to enable Invoice Settlement, see [Invoice Settlement Enablement and Checklist Guide](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement/Invoice_Settlement_Migration_Checklist_and_Guide) for more information.<br>|

## Invoice and collect

<a id="opIdPOST_TransactionInvoicePayment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/operations/invoice-collect \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "accountKey": "4028925a4cb74ec9014cb7520fc00005",
    "invoiceId": "4028925a4cb74ec9014cb7540988002e",
    "paymentGateway": "TestGateway"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/operations/invoice-collect`

Generates and posts invoices and credit memos and collects payments for posted invoices. Credit memos are only available if you have the Invoice Settlement feature enabled and negative charges exist. Credit memos will not be applied to invoices. If draft invoices and credit memos exist when you run this operation, this operation will post the invoices and credit memos. Note that draft credit memos created from an invoice or a product rate plan charge will not be posted.

You can use this operation to generate invoices and collect payments on the posted invoices,
 or else simply collect payment on a specified existing
invoice. The customer's default payment method is used, and the full
amount due is collected. The operation depends on the parameters you
specify.

- To generate one or more new invoices for that customer and collect
payment on the generated and other unpaid invoice(s), leave the **invoiceId** field empty. 

- To collect payment on an existing invoice, specify the invoice ID. 


The operation is atomic; if any part is unsuccessful, the entire
operation is rolled back.

When an error occurs, gateway reason codes and error messages are returned the error response of this operation. The following items are some gateway response code examples.

- Orbital: `05 Do Not Honor`; `14 Invalid Credit Card Number`
- Vantiv: `301 Invalid Account Number`; `304 Lost/Stolen Card`  
- CyberSource2: `202 Expired card`; `231 Invalid account number`

For more reason code information, see the corresponding payment gateway documentation. 


## Notes

Timeouts may occur when using this method on an account that
has an extremely high number of subscriptions.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "accountKey": "4028925a4cb74ec9014cb7520fc00005",
  "invoiceId": "4028925a4cb74ec9014cb7540988002e",
  "paymentGateway": "TestGateway"
}
```

<h3 id="invoice-and-collect-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|zuora-version|header|string|false|<br>The minor version of the Zuora REST API. <br><br>You need to set this parameter if you use the following fields:<br>* documentDate<br>* targetDate            <br><br>If you have the Invoice Settlement feature enabled, you need to specify this parameter. Otherwise, an error is returned.<br><br><br>See [Zuora REST API Versions](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#section/API-Versions) for more information.<br>|
|body|body|[POSTInvoiceCollectType](#schemapostinvoicecollecttype)|true|none|
|» accountKey|body|string|true|Customer account ID or account number.<br>|
|» documentDate|body|string(date)|false|The date that should appear on the invoice and credit memo being generated,<br>in `yyyy-mm-dd` format. If this field is omitted<br>and `invoiceId` is not specified, the current date is used by default. <br><br><br>**Note:** The credit memo is only available if you have the Invoice Settlement feature enabled.<br><br><br>This field is in Zuora REST API version control. Supported minor<br>versions are `215.0` and later. To use this field in the method, you<br>must set the  `zuora-version` parameter to the minor version number in<br>the request header.<br>|
|» invoiceDate|body|string(date)|false|**Note:** This field has been replaced by the `documentDate` field in Zuora REST API version `215.0` and later. The<br>`invoiceDate` field is only available for backward<br>compatibility.<br><br>The date that should appear on the invoice being generated,<br>in `yyyy-mm-dd` format. If this field is omitted<br>and `invoiceId` is not specified, the current date is used by default. <br><br>This field is in Zuora REST API version control. Supported minor<br>versions are `214.0` and earlier.<br>|
|» invoiceId|body|string|false|The ID of an existing invoice for which to collect payment using<br>the account's default payment method. If this value is specified, no new<br>invoice is generated, and the following fields are ignored:<br>  - `invoiceDate` and `invoiceTargetDate` (if the Zuora REST API version is 214.0 or earlier)<br>  - `documentDate` and `targetDate` (if the Zuora REST API version is 215.0 or later)<br>|
|» invoiceTargetDate|body|string(date)|false|**Note:** This field has been replaced by the `targetDate` field in Zuora REST API version `215.0` and later. The<br>`invoiceTargetDate` field is only available for backward<br>compatibility.<br><br><br>The date through which to calculate charges on this account if an invoice is generated, in `yyyy-mm-dd` format. If this field is omitted<br>and `invoiceId` is not specified, the current date is used by default. <br><br><br>This field is in Zuora REST API version control. Supported minor<br>versions are `214.0` and earlier.  <br>|
|» paymentGateway|body|string|false|The name of the gateway that will be used for the payment. Must be a valid gateway name and the gateway must support the specific payment method. If a value is not specified, the default gateway on the Account will be used.<br>|
|» targetDate|body|string(date)|false|The date through which to calculate charges on this account if an invoice or a credit memo is generated, <br>in `yyyy-mm-dd` format. If this field is omitted<br>and `invoiceId` is not specified, the current date is used by default. <br><br><br>**Note:** The credit memo is only available if you have the Invoice Settlement feature enabled.<br><br><br>This field is in Zuora REST API version control. Supported minor<br>versions are `215.0` and later. To use this field in the method, you<br>must set the  `zuora-version` parameter to the minor version number in<br>the request header.<br>|

|200|Zuora-Request-Id|string||The Zuora internal identifier of the API call. You cannot control the value of this header.<br>|
|200|Zuora-Track-Id|string||A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you specified a tracing identifier in the request headers, Zuora returns the same tracing identifier. Otherwise, Zuora does not set this header.<br>|

<h1 id="api-reference-billing-orders">Orders</h1>

## Retrieve the status and response of a job

<a id="opIdGET_JobStatusAndResponse"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/async-jobs/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v1/async-jobs/{jobId}`

**Note:** This operation is only available if you have the [Orders](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BC_Subscription_Management/Orders/AA_Overview_of_Orders#Orders) feature enabled. Orders is now generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 284 (August 2020). If you are an existing Zuora Subscribe and Amend customer and want to adopt Orders, see [What is Orders Harmonization](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Orders_Harmonization/Orders_Harmonization#What_is_Orders_Harmonization.3F) and join the [Orders Harmonization community group](https://community.zuora.com/t5/Orders-Harmonization/gp-p/Orders-Harmonization) for more information. If you want to enable Orders, submit a request at [Zuora Global Support](https://support.zuora.com/).

**Note:** The [Order Line Items](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Order_Line_Items/AA_Overview_of_Order_Line_Items) feature is in the **Early Adopter** phase. We are actively soliciting feedback from a small set of early adopters before releasing it as generally available. If you want to join this early adopter program, submit a request at [Zuora Global Support](https://support.zuora.com/).

Get the status and response of an asynchronous job. Currently, an asynchronous job created by "Create an order asynchronously" or "Preview an order asynchronously" is supported.


<h3 id="retrieve-the-status-and-response-of-a-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|jobId|path|string(UUID)|true|UUID of the asynchronous job created by an asynchronous API operation.|

`POST /v1/async/orders`

**Note:** This operation is only available if you have the [Orders](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BC_Subscription_Management/Orders/AA_Overview_of_Orders#Orders) feature enabled. Orders is now generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 284 (August 2020). If you are an existing Zuora Subscribe and Amend customer and want to adopt Orders, see [What is Orders Harmonization](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Orders_Harmonization/Orders_Harmonization#What_is_Orders_Harmonization.3F) and join the [Orders Harmonization community group](https://community.zuora.com/t5/Orders-Harmonization/gp-p/Orders-Harmonization) for more information. If you want to enable Orders, submit a request at [Zuora Global Support](https://support.zuora.com/).

**Note:** The [Order Line Items](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Order_Line_Items/AA_Overview_of_Order_Line_Items) feature is in the **Early Adopter** phase. We are actively soliciting feedback from a small set of early adopters before releasing it as generally available. If you want to join this early adopter program, submit a request at [Zuora Global Support](https://support.zuora.com/).


In the case where a normal "Create an order" operation call will time out, use this operation instead to create an order asynchronously. A job will be creating the order in the back end; the job ID will be returned for tracking the job status and result. 

The limit of orders allowed on a subscription is 1000.

The limit of order line items allowed in an order is 100.

Zuora has the following limits on the Orders synchronous API to prevent performance degradation: 
* Up to 50 subscriptions are allowed in a single [Create an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_Order) or [Preview an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrder) operation call.
* Up to 50 order actions are allowed in a single [Create an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_Order) or [Preview an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrder) operation call.
* Up to 50 order actions are allowed on a single subscription in a [Create an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_Order) or [Preview an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrder) operation call.

If you have an Order that exceeds any limits of the above, Zuora recommends you use the following asynchronous API operations:
* [Create an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_CreateOrderAsynchronously)
* [Preview an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrderAsynchronously)

Zuora has the following limits on the Orders asynchronous API operations to prevent performance degradation:
* Up to 300 subscriptions are allowed in a single [Create an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_CreateOrderAsynchronously) or [Preview an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrderAsynchronously) operation call.
* Up to 300 order actions are allowed in a single [Create an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_CreateOrderAsynchronously) or [Preview an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrderAsynchronously) operation call.
* Up to 300 order actions are allowed on a single subscription in a [Create an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_CreateOrderAsynchronously) or [Preview an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrderAsynchronously) operation call.

If you have a need for a large order that exceeds any limits of the above, you can request a limit increase for the Orders asynchronous API by submitting a request at [Zuora Global Support](https://support.zuora.com).

<h3 id="create-an-order-asynchronously-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|returnIds|query|boolean|false|Specify whether to return IDs for the [Get job status and response](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/GET_JobStatusAndResponse) operation. If you set this query parameter to `true`, the corresponding IDs, which are associated with the numbers returned in this operation, can be returned in the "Get job status and response" response body.<br>|
|zuora-version|header|string|false|<br>The minor version of the Zuora REST API. <br><br>You need to set this parameter if you want to use the following fields:<br>* subscriptions<br>* subscriptionNumbers<br>* subscriptionIds (when the `returnId` query parameter is set to `true`)<br>|
|body|body|[POSTOrderRequestType](#schemapostorderrequesttype)|true|none|
|» customFields|body|[OrderObjectCustomFields](#schemaorderobjectcustomfields)|false|Container for custom fields of an Order object.<br>|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the order.|
|» existingAccountNumber|body|string|false|The account number that this order will be created under. It can be either the accountNumber or the account info provided. It will return an error if both are specified.<br>Note that this actually specifies the invoice owner account of the subscriptions included in this order.<br>|
|» newAccount|body|[Account](#schemaaccount)|false|none|
|» orderDate|body|string(date)|true|The date when the order is signed. All the order actions under this order will use this order date as the contract effective date if the contract effective date field is skipped or its value is left as null.|
|» orderLineItems|body|[[CreateOrderOrderLineItem](#schemacreateorderorderlineitem)]|false|[Order Line Items](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Order_Line_Items/AA_Overview_of_Order_Line_Items) are non subscription based items created by an Order, representing transactional charges such as one-time fees, physical goods, or professional service charges that are not sold as subscription services. <br><br>With the Order Line Items feature enabled, you can now launch non-subscription and hybrid monetization business models in Zuora, in addition to subscription business models.<br><br>**Note:** The [Order Line Items](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Order_Line_Items/AA_Overview_of_Order_Line_Items) feature is in the **Early Adopter** phase. We are actively soliciting feedback from a small set of early adopters before releasing it as generally available. If you want to join this early adopter program, submit a request at [Zuora Global Support](https://support.zuora.com/). <br>|
|» orderNumber|body|string|false|The order number of the new order. If not provided, system will auto-generate a number for this order.|
|» processingOptions|body|[ProcessingOptions](#schemaprocessingoptions)|false|Invoice or Payment.|
|» subscriptions|body|[object]|true|Each item includes a set of order actions, which will be applied to the same base subscription.|
|» » customFields|body|[SubscriptionObjectCustomFields](#schemasubscriptionobjectcustomfields)|false|Container for custom fields of a Subscription object.<br>|
|» » orderActions|body|[[CreateOrderOrderAction](#schemacreateorderorderaction)]|false|The actions to be applied to the subscription. Order actions will be stored with the sequence when it was provided in the request.|
|» » quote|body|[QuoteObjectFields](#schemaquoteobjectfields)|false|The fields populated for a quote when a quote is sent to Zuora Billing from Zuora Quote.<br>|
|» » ramp|body|[RampRequest](#schemaramprequest)|false|Container of the ramp definitions. It is used to create, update, or remove the ramp definition for the new subscription.<br>|
|» » subscriptionNumber|body|string|false|Leave this empty to represent new subscription creation. Specify a subscription number to update an existing subscription.<br>|

`POST /v1/async/orders/preview`

**Note:** This operation is only available if you have the [Orders](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BC_Subscription_Management/Orders/AA_Overview_of_Orders#Orders) feature enabled. Orders is now generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 284 (August 2020). If you are an existing Zuora Subscribe and Amend customer and want to adopt Orders, see [What is Orders Harmonization](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Orders_Harmonization/Orders_Harmonization#What_is_Orders_Harmonization.3F) and join the [Orders Harmonization community group](https://community.zuora.com/t5/Orders-Harmonization/gp-p/Orders-Harmonization) for more information. If you want to enable Orders, submit a request at [Zuora Global Support](https://support.zuora.com/).

**Note:** The [Order Line Items](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Order_Line_Items/AA_Overview_of_Order_Line_Items) feature is in the **Early Adopter** phase. We are actively soliciting feedback from a small set of early adopters before releasing it as generally available. If you want to join this early adopter program, submit a request at [Zuora Global Support](https://support.zuora.com/).       

In the case where a normal "Preview an order" operation call will time out, use this operation instead to preview an order asynchronously. A job will be previewing the order in the back end; the job ID will be returned for tracking the job status and result.

The limit of orders allowed on a subscription is 1000.

The limit of order line items allowed in an order is 100.

Zuora has the following limits on the Orders synchronous API to prevent performance degradation: 
* Up to 50 subscriptions are allowed in a single [Create an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_Order) or [Preview an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrder) operation call.
* Up to 50 order actions are allowed in a single [Create an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_Order) or [Preview an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrder) operation call.
* Up to 50 order actions are allowed on a single subscription in a [Create an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_Order) or [Preview an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrder) operation call.

If you have an Order that exceeds any limits of the above, Zuora recommends you use the following asynchronous API operations:
* [Create an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_CreateOrderAsynchronously)
* [Preview an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrderAsynchronously)

Zuora has the following limits on the Orders asynchronous API operations to prevent performance degradation:
* Up to 300 subscriptions are allowed in a single [Create an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_CreateOrderAsynchronously) or [Preview an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrderAsynchronously) operation call.
* Up to 300 order actions are allowed in a single [Create an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_CreateOrderAsynchronously) or [Preview an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrderAsynchronously) operation call.
* Up to 300 order actions are allowed on a single subscription in a [Create an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_CreateOrderAsynchronously) or [Preview an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrderAsynchronously) operation call.

If you have a need for a large order that exceeds any limits of the above, you can request a limit increase for the Orders asynchronous API by submitting a request at [Zuora Global Support](https://support.zuora.com).

<h3 id="preview-an-order-asynchronously-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|body|body|[POSTOrderPreviewRequestType](#schemapostorderpreviewrequesttype)|true|none|
|» customFields|body|[OrderObjectCustomFields](#schemaorderobjectcustomfields)|false|Container for custom fields of an Order object.<br>|
|» description|body|string|false|A description of the order.|
|» existingAccountNumber|body|string|false|The account number that this order will be created under. It can be either the accountNumber or the account info. It will return an error if both are specified.<br>Note that invoice owner account of the subscriptions included in this order should be the same with the account of the order.<br>|
|» orderDate|body|string(date)|true|The date when the order is signed. All of the order actions under this order will use this order date as the contract effective date.|
|» orderLineItems|body|[[CreateOrderOrderLineItem](#schemacreateorderorderlineitem)]|false|[Order Line Items](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Order_Line_Items/AA_Overview_of_Order_Line_Items) are non subscription based items created by an Order, representing transactional charges such as one-time fees, physical goods, or professional service charges that are not sold as subscription services. <br><br>With the Order Line Items feature enabled, you can now launch non-subscription and hybrid monetization business models in Zuora, in addition to subscription business models. <br><br>**Note:** The [Order Line Items](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Order_Line_Items/AA_Overview_of_Order_Line_Items) feature is in the **Early Adopter** phase. We are actively soliciting feedback from a small set of early adopters before releasing it as generally available. If you want to join this early adopter program, submit a request at [Zuora Global Support](https://support.zuora.com/). <br>|
|» orderNumber|body|string|false|The order number of this order.|
|» previewAccountInfo|body|[PreviewAccountInfo](#schemapreviewaccountinfo)|false|Information about the account that will own the order.<br>|
|» previewOptions|body|[PreviewOptions](#schemapreviewoptions)|true|none|
|» subscriptions|body|[object]|true|Each item includes a set of order actions, which will be applied to the same base subscription.|
|» » customFields|body|[SubscriptionObjectCustomFields](#schemasubscriptionobjectcustomfields)|false|Container for custom fields of a Subscription object.<br>|
|» » orderActions|body|[[PreviewOrderOrderAction](#schemaprevieworderorderaction)]|false|The actions to be applied to the subscription. Order actions will be stored with the sequence when it was provided in the request.|
|» » quote|body|[QuoteObjectFields](#schemaquoteobjectfields)|false|The fields populated for a quote when a quote is sent to Zuora Billing from Zuora Quote.<br>|
|» » ramp|body|[RampRequest](#schemaramprequest)|false|Container of the ramp definitions. It is used to create, update, or remove the ramp definition for the new subscription.<br>|
|» » subscriptionNumber|body|string|false|Leave this field empty to represent new subscription creation, or specify a subscription number to update an existing subscription.<br>|

## List orders

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/orders \
```

`GET /v1/orders`

**Note:** This feature is only available if you have the [Order Metrics](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BC_Subscription_Management/Orders/AA_Overview_of_Orders#Order_Metrics) feature enabled. As of Zuora Billing Release 284, Orders is generally available and the Order Metrics feature is no longer available as a standalone feature. If you are an existing Subscribe and Amend customer and want Order Metrics only, you must turn on [Orders Harmonization](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Orders_Harmonization/Orders_Harmonization). You can still keep the existing Subscribe and Amend API integrations to create and manage subscriptions.

**Note:** The [Order Line Items](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Order_Line_Items/AA_Overview_of_Order_Line_Items) feature is in the **Early Adopter** phase. We are actively soliciting feedback from a small set of early adopters before releasing it as generally available. If you want to join this early adopter program, submit a request at [Zuora Global Support](https://support.zuora.com/).


Retrieves information about all orders in your tenant. By default, it returns the first page of the orders. 


<h3 id="list-orders-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|page|query|integer|false|The page number of the orders retrieved. <br>|
|pageSize|query|integer|false|Number of rows returned per page.<br>|
|dateFilterOption|query|string|false|The date type to filter on. This field value can be orderDate or updatedDate. Default is orderDate.<br>|
|startDate|query|string(date)|false|The result will only contain the orders with the date of dateFilterOption later than or equal to this date.<br>|
|endDate|query|string(date)|false|The result will only contains orders with the date of dateFilterOption earlier than or equal to this date.<br>|

`POST /v1/orders`

**Note:** This operation is only available if you have the [Orders](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BC_Subscription_Management/Orders/AA_Overview_of_Orders#Orders) feature enabled. Orders is now generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 284 (August 2020). If you are an existing Zuora Subscribe and Amend customer and want to adopt Orders, see [What is Orders Harmonization](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Orders_Harmonization/Orders_Harmonization#What_is_Orders_Harmonization.3F) and join the [Orders Harmonization community group](https://community.zuora.com/t5/Orders-Harmonization/gp-p/Orders-Harmonization) for more information. If you want to enable Orders, submit a request at [Zuora Global Support](https://support.zuora.com/).

**Note:** The [Order Line Items](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Order_Line_Items/AA_Overview_of_Order_Line_Items) feature is in the **Early Adopter** phase. We are actively soliciting feedback from a small set of early adopters before releasing it as generally available. If you want to join this early adopter program, submit a request at [Zuora Global Support](https://support.zuora.com/).

You can use this operation to create subscriptions and make changes to subscriptions by creating orders. You can also use this operation to create order line items by creating orders. The following tutorials demonstrate how to use this operation:

 * [Create a Subscription](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BC_Subscription_Management/Orders/AC_Orders_Tutorials/A_Create_a_Subscription)
 * [Add a Product to a Subscription](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BC_Subscription_Management/Orders/AC_Orders_Tutorials/A_Add_a_Product_to_a_Subscription)
 * [Create a Ramp Deal](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Ramps_and_Ramp_Metrics/B_Create_a_Ramp_Deal)
 * [Add a Product Mid-Interval Update on a Ramp Deal](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Ramps_and_Ramp_Metrics/E_Update_a_Product_in_a_Ramp_Deal)
 * [Add a Product in a Ramp Deal](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Ramps_and_Ramp_Metrics/C_Add_a_Product_in_a_Ramp_Deal)
 * [Change the Terms and Conditions of a Ramp Deal](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Ramps_and_Ramp_Metrics/D_Change_the_Terms_and_Conditions_of_a_Ramp_Deal_and_Update_the_Ramp)
 * [Change the Owner of a Subscription](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BC_Subscription_Management/Orders/AC_Orders_Tutorials/C_Change_the_Owner_of_a_Subscription)
 * [Change the Terms and Conditions of a Subscription](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BC_Subscription_Management/Orders/AC_Orders_Tutorials/C_Change_the_Terms_and_Conditions_of_a_Subscription)
 * [Renew a Subscription](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BC_Subscription_Management/Orders/AC_Orders_Tutorials/C_Renew_a_Subscription)
 * [Renew a Subscription and Upgrade a Product](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BC_Subscription_Management/Orders/AC_Orders_Tutorials/C_Renew_a_Subscription_and_Upgrade_a_Product)
 * [Replace a Product in a Subscription](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BC_Subscription_Management/Orders/AC_Orders_Tutorials/C_Replace_a_Product_in_a_Subscription)
 * [Update a Product in a Subscription](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BC_Subscription_Management/Orders/AC_Orders_Tutorials/C_Update_a_Product_in_a_Subscription)
 * [Cancel a Subscription](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BC_Subscription_Management/Orders/AC_Orders_Tutorials/D_Cancel_a_Subscription)
 * [Remove a Product from a Subscription](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BC_Subscription_Management/Orders/AC_Orders_Tutorials/D_Remove_a_Product_from_a_Subscription)
 * [Create an order line item](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Order_Line_Items/Create_an_order_line_item)
 * [Create an order line item with a new subscription](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Subscriptions/Orders/Order_Line_Items/Create_an_order_line_item_with_a_new_subscription)

You can also see the [API Guides](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-guides/) for more use cases of the "Create an order" operation.

Creating a draft order is currently not supported. See [Known Limitations in Orders](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BC_Subscription_Management/Orders/C_Known_Limitations_in_Orders) for additional limitations.

The limit of orders allowed on a subscription is 1000.

The limit of order line items allowed in an order is 100.

Zuora has the following limits on the Orders synchronous API to prevent performance degradation: 
* Up to 50 subscriptions are allowed in a single [Create an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_Order) or [Preview an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrder) operation call.
* Up to 50 order actions are allowed in a single [Create an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_Order) or [Preview an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrder) operation call.
* Up to 50 order actions are allowed on a single subscription in a [Create an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_Order) or [Preview an order](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrder) operation call.

If you have an Order that exceeds any limits of the above, Zuora recommends you use the following asynchronous API operations:
* [Create an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_CreateOrderAsynchronously)
* [Preview an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrderAsynchronously)

Zuora has the following limits on the Orders asynchronous API operations to prevent performance degradation:
* Up to 300 subscriptions are allowed in a single [Create an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_CreateOrderAsynchronously) or [Preview an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrderAsynchronously) operation call.
* Up to 300 order actions are allowed in a single [Create an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_CreateOrderAsynchronously) or [Preview an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrderAsynchronously) operation call.
* Up to 300 order actions are allowed on a single subscription in a [Create an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_CreateOrderAsynchronously) or [Preview an order asynchronously](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/POST_PreviewOrderAsynchronously) operation call.

If you have a need for a large order that exceeds any limits of the above, you can request a limit increase for the Orders asynchronous API by submitting a request at [Zuora Global Support](https://support.zuora.com).        

**Note:** When you are to suspend a subcription (via the `suspend` order action), if in the same "Create an order" call you are to perform other subsequent order actions on the supscription to suspend, you must first resume the subscription (via a `resume` order action). 

**Note:** When using this operation to create an account, create a subscription, run billing, and collect payment in a single call, if any error occurs during the call, such as a payment processing failure and a tax engine failure, then all the other steps will be rolled back. This means that the invoice will not be generated, the subscription will not be created, and the account will not be created.
