## Create a stored credential profile

<a id="opIdPOST_CreateStoredCredentialProfile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment-methods/string/profiles \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "authGateway": "4028905f5702783601570291e14c0015",
    "consentAgreementRef": "ACCT1338AgreementV1.pdf",
    "consentAgreementSrc": "External",
    "status": "Active",
    "type": "Recurring"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/payment-methods/{payment-method-id}/profiles`

Creates a stored credential profile within a payment method.

The stored credential profile represents a consent agreement that you have established with a customer. When you use the payment method in a transaction, Zuora may include information from the stored credential profile to inform the payment processor that the transaction is related to your pre-existing consent agreement with the customer.

**Note:** This feature is in the **Early Adopters** phase. We are actively soliciting feedback from a small set of early adopters before releasing as generally available.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "authGateway": "4028905f5702783601570291e14c0015",
  "consentAgreementRef": "ACCT1338AgreementV1.pdf",
  "consentAgreementSrc": "External",
  "status": "Active",
  "type": "Recurring"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-stored-credential-profile-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|payment-method-id|path|string|true|ID of a payment method.<br>|
|body|body|[CreateStoredCredentialProfileRequest](#schemacreatestoredcredentialprofilerequest)|true|none|
|» action|body|string|false|Specifies how Zuora activates the stored credential profile. Only applicable if you set the `status` field to `Active`.<br><br>* `Activate` (default) - Use this value if you are creating the stored credential profile after receiving the customer's consent.<br><br>  Zuora will create the stored credential profile then send a cardholder-initiated transaction (CIT) to the payment gateway to validate the stored credential profile. If the CIT succeeds, the status of the stored credential profile will be `Active`. If the CIT does not succeed, Zuora will not create a stored credential profile.<br>  <br>  If the payment gateway does not support the stored credential transaction framework, the status of the stored credential profile will be `Agreed`.<br><br><br>* `Persist` - Use this value if the stored credential profile represents a stored credential profile in an external system. The status of the payment method's stored credential profile will be `Active`.<br>|
|» agreedOn|body|string(date)|false|The date on which the profile is agreed. The date format is `yyyy-mm-dd`.<br>|
|» authGateway|body|string|false|Specifies the ID of the payment gateway that Zuora will use when activating the stored credential profile.<br>|
|» cardSecurityCode|body|string|false|The security code of the credit card.<br>|
|» consentAgreementRef|body|string|false|Specifies your reference for the consent agreement that you have established with the customer.<br>|
|» consentAgreementSrc|body|string|true|none|
|» networkTransactionId|body|string|false|The ID of a network transaction.<br>|
|» status|body|string|true|Specifies the status of the stored credential profile.<br><br>* `Active` - Use this value if you are creating the stored credential profile after receiving the customer's consent, or if the stored credential profile represents a stored credential profile in an external system.<br><br>  You can use the `action` field to specify how Zuora activates the stored credential profile.<br><br><br>* `Agreed` - Use this value if you are migrating the payment method to the stored credential transaction framework.<br><br>  In this case, Zuora will not send a cardholder-initiated transaction (CIT) to the payment gateway to validate the stored credential profile.<br>|
|» type|body|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|Activate|
|» action|Persist|
|» consentAgreementSrc|External|
|» status|Agreed|
|» status|Active|
|» type|Recurring|
|» type|Unscheduled|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "number": 3,
  "paymentMethodId": "402881836953a3c7016953aec290000d",
  "success": true
}
```

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment-methods/string/scrub \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`PUT /v1/payment-methods/{payment-method-id}/scrub`


This operation enables you to replace all sensitive data in a payment method, related payment method snapshot table, and four related log tables with dummy values that will be stored in Zuora databases. 

This operation will scrub the sensitive data and soft-delete the specified payment method at the same time. 

If you want to delete or anonymize personal data in Zuora, you must scrub the payment method before anonymizing the associated account and contact. See [Delete or anonymize personal data](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Responding_to_individual_requests_for_access%2C_correction%2C_and_deletion_of_data_under_applicable_privacy_laws#Edit_and_correct_personal_data) for more information.

**Note:** In order to use this operation, you must ensure that the **Scrub Sensitive Data of Specific Payment Method payments** permission is enabled in your user role. Contact your tenant administrator if you want to enable this permission. See [Scrub Payment Methods](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/CB_Billing/L_Payment_Methods/Scrub_Payment_Methods) for more information.


<h3 id="scrub-a-payment-method-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|payment-method-id|path|string|true|The ID of the payment method where you want to scrub the sensitive data.<br>|

```json
{
  "success": true
}
```

## Verify a payment method

<a id="opIdPUT_VerifyPaymentMethods"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment-methods/string/verify \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "gatewayOptions": {
      "Comments": "test",
      "IPAddress": "192.168.1.1"
    },
    "paymentGatewayName": "Adyen",
    "securityCode": "737"
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/payment-methods/{payment-method-id}/verify`

Sends an authorization request to the corresponding payment gateway to verify the payment method, even though no changes are made for the payment method. Supported payment methods are Credit Cards and Paypal.

Zuora now supports performing a standalone zero dollar verification or one dollar authorization for credit cards. It also supports a billing agreement status check on PayPal payment methods.

If a payment method is created by Hosted Payment Pages and is not assigned to any billing account, the payment method cannot be verified through this operation.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "gatewayOptions": {
    "Comments": "test",
    "IPAddress": "192.168.1.1"
  },
  "paymentGatewayName": "Adyen",
  "securityCode": "737"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|payment-method-id|path|string|true|The ID of the payment method to be verified.<br>|
|body|body|[PUTVerifyPaymentMethodType](#schemaputverifypaymentmethodtype)|true|none|
|» currencyCode|body|string|false|The currency used for payment method authorization. <br>|
|» gatewayOptions|body|object|false|The field used to pass gateway-specific parameters and parameter values.<br>|
|» » key|body|string|false|The name of a gateway-specific parameter.<br>|
|» » value|body|string|false|The value of the gateway-specific parameter.<br>|
|» paymentGatewayName|body|string|false|The name of the payment gateway instance. If no value is specified for this field, the default payment gateway of the customer account will be used.<br>|
|» securityCode|body|string|false|The CVV or CVV2 security code for the credit card or debit card. To ensure PCI compliance, the value of this field is not stored and cannot be queried.<br>|

<h1 id="api-reference-billing-payment-runs">Payment Runs</h1>

## List payment runs

<a id="opIdGET_PaymentRuns"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment-runs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v1/payment-runs`

Retrieves the information about all payment runs. You can define filterable fields to restrict the data returned in the response.

### Filtering

You can use query parameters to restrict the data returned in the response. Each query parameter corresponds to one field in the response body.

If the value of a filterable field is string, you can set the corresponding query parameter to `null` when filtering. Then, you can get the response data with this field value being `null`. 

Examples:

- /v1/payment-runs?status=Processed

- /v1/payment-runs?targetDate=2017-10-10&status=Pending

- /v1/payment-runs?status=Completed&sort=+updatedDate


<h3 id="list-payment-runs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|pageSize|query|integer|false|Number of rows returned per page.<br>|
|createdById|query|string|false|This parameter filters the response based on the `createdById` field.<br>|
|createdDate|query|string(date-time)|false|This parameter filters the response based on the `createdDate` field.<br>|
|status|query|string|false|This parameter filters the response based on the `status` field.<br>|
|targetDate|query|string(date)|false|This parameter filters the response based on the `targetDate` field.<br>|
|updatedById|query|string|false|This parameter filters the response based on the `updatedById` field.<br>|
|updatedDate|query|string(date-time)|false|This parameter filters the response based on the `updatedDate` field.<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|This parameter restricts the order of the data returned in the response. You can use this parameter to supply a dimension you want to sort on.<br><br>A sortable field uses the following form: <br><br>*operator* *field_name*<br><br>You can use at most two sortable fields in one URL path. Use a comma to separate sortable fields. For example:  *operator* *field_name*, *operator* *field_name*  <br><br>*operator* is used to mark the order of sequencing. The operator is optional. If you only specify the sortable field without any operator, the response data is sorted in descending order by this field.<br><br>  - The `-` operator indicates an ascending order.<br>  - The `+` operator indicates a descending order.<br><br>By default, the response data is displayed in descending order by payment run number.<br><br>*field_name* indicates the name of a sortable field. The supported sortable fields of this operation are as below:<br><br>  - targetDate<br>  - status<br>  - createdDate<br>  - createdById<br>  - updatedDate<br>  - updatedById<br><br>Examples:<br><br>- /v1/payment-runs?sort=+createdDate<br><br>- /v1/payment-runs?status=Processing&sort=-createdById,+targetDate<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|Pending|
|status|Processing|
|status|Completed|
|status|Error|
|status|Canceled|

```json
  "nextPage": "/payment-runs?page=2",

    {
      "applyCreditBalance": false,

      "completedOn": "2017-12-28 13:00:00",
      "consolidatedPayment": false,
      "createdById": "2c92c0f956bc8fcb0156f8eee04b4d54",
```

## Create a payment run

<a id="opIdPOST_PaymentRun"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment-runs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "accountId": "402890245f097f39015f0e9fcdd60558",
    "autoApplyCreditMemo": "true",
    "autoApplyUnappliedPayment": "true",
    "consolidatedPayment": "true",
    "processPaymentWithClosedPM": "true",
    "targetDate": "2017-10-10"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/payment-runs`

Creates a payment run. You can create a payment run to be executed immediately after it is created, or a scheduled payment run to be executed in future.

To filter the payments to be collected for a payment run, you can use either of the following methods but not both:

  - Use the `accountId`, `batch`, `billCycleDay`, `currency`, `paymentGatewayId`, and `billingRunId` fields to define the billing documents to be collected.
  - Use the `data` field to specify the records of accounts and billing documents to be collected, in a more flexible manner.

If no filter criteria are specified in the request body, the payment run collects payments for all accounts.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "accountId": "402890245f097f39015f0e9fcdd60558",
  "autoApplyCreditMemo": "true",
  "autoApplyUnappliedPayment": "true",
  "consolidatedPayment": "true",
  "processPaymentWithClosedPM": "true",
  "targetDate": "2017-10-10"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-payment-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|body|body|[POSTPaymentRunRequest](#schemapostpaymentrunrequest)|true|none|
|» accountId|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of the customer account associated with the payment run.<br><br>This field conflicts with each of the `batch`, `billCycleDay`, `currency`, `paymentGatewayId`, and `billingRunId` fields. If there are such conflicts, an error occurs and an error message is returned.<br>|
|» applyCreditBalance|body|boolean|false|**Note:** This field is only available if you have the Credit Balance feature enabled and the Invoice Settlement feature disabled.<br><br>Whether to apply credit balances in the payment run. This field is only available when you have Invoice Settlement feature disabled.<br>|
|» autoApplyCreditMemo|body|boolean|false|**Note:** This field is only available if you have [Invoice Settlement](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement) enabled. The Invoice Settlement feature is generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 296 (March 2021). This feature includes Unapplied Payments, Credit and Debit Memo, and Invoice Item Settlement. If you want to enable Invoice Settlement, see [Invoice Settlement Enablement and Checklist Guide](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement/Invoice_Settlement_Migration_Checklist_and_Guide) for more information.<br><br>Whether to automatically apply a posted credit memo to one or more receivables in the payment run.<br>|
|» autoApplyUnappliedPayment|body|boolean|false|**Note:** This field is only available if you have [Invoice Settlement](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement) enabled. The Invoice Settlement feature is generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 296 (March 2021). This feature includes Unapplied Payments, Credit and Debit Memo, and Invoice Item Settlement. If you want to enable Invoice Settlement, see [Invoice Settlement Enablement and Checklist Guide](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement/Invoice_Settlement_Migration_Checklist_and_Guide) for more information.<br><br>Whether to automatically apply unapplied payments to  one or more receivables in the payment run.<br>|
|» batch|body|string|false|The alias name given to a batch. The batch name is a string of 50 characters or less.<br><br>This field conflicts with the `accountId` field. If they are both specified in the request body, an error occurs and an error message is returned. <br>|
|» billCycleDay|body|string|false|The billing cycle day (BCD), the day of the month when a bill run generates invoices for the account. The value must be equal to or less then 31, and 31 is mean the EOM.<br><br>This field conflicts with the `accountId` field. If they are both specified in the request body, an error occurs and an error message is returned.<br>|
|» billingRunId|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of a bill run.<br><br>This field conflicts with the `accountId` field. If they are both specified in the request body, an error occurs and an error message is returned.<br>|
|» collectPayment|body|boolean|false|Whether to process electronic payments during the execution of payment runs. <br><br>If the Payment user permission "Process Electronic Payment" is disabled, this field will be ignored.<br>|
|» consolidatedPayment|body|boolean|false|**Note:** The **Process Electronic Payment** permission also needs to be allowed for a Manage Payment Runs role to work. See [Payments Roles](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/CF_Users_and_Administrators/A_Administrator_Settings/User_Roles/e_Payments_Roles) for more information. <br><br>Whether to process a single payment for all receivables that are due on an account.<br>|
|» currency|body|string|false|A currency defined in the web-based UI administrative settings.<br><br>This field conflicts with the `accountId` field. If they are both specified in the request body, an error occurs and an error message is returned.<br>|
|» data|body|[[POSTPaymentRunDataElementRequest](#schemapostpaymentrundataelementrequest)]|false|<br>The array of data for specifying records of accounts and invoices/debit memos that will be collected and processed by a payment run. A maximum of 50K records are allowed to be passed into the `data` array.<br><br>Here is an example:<br>```<br>  {<br>    "accountId": "60c81b5bc51649e8a7d1b48303194790",<br>    "documentId": "2c9081a03c63c94c013c6894af5602dd",<br>    "documentType": "Invoice",<br>    "amount": 80,<br>    "paymentMethodId": "2c9081a03c6d7b51013c6d7e4ada0a1c",<br>    "paymentGatewayId": "d2abe8342e1811ea80e774b9452e17ea",<br>    "comment": "Payment Comments"<br>  }<br>```<br>|
|» paymentGatewayId|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of the gateway instance that processes the payment.<br><br>This field conflicts with the `accountId` field. If they are both specified in the request body, an error occurs and an error message is returned.<br>|
|» processPaymentWithClosedPM|body|boolean|false|**Note:** The **Process Electronic Payment** permission also needs to be allowed for a Manage Payment Runs role to work. See [Payments Roles](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/CF_Users_and_Administrators/A_Administrator_Settings/User_Roles/e_Payments_Roles) for more information. <br><br>Whether to process payments even if the default payment method is closed.<br>|
|» runDate|body|string(date-time)|false|The date and time when the scheduled payment run is to be executed, in `yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss` format. The backend will ignore mintues and seconds in the field value. For example, if you specify `2017-03-01 11:30:37` for this value, this payment run will be run at 2017-03-01 11:00:00.<br><br>You must specify either the `runDate` field or the `targetDate` field in the request body. If you specify the `runDate` field, the scheduced payment run is to be executed on the run date. If you specify the `targetDate` field, the payment run is executed immediately after it is created. <br>|
|» targetDate|body|string(date)|false|The target date used to determine which receivables to be paid in the payment run. The payments are collected for all receivables with the due date no later than the target date.<br><br>You must specify either the `runDate` field or the `targetDate` field in the request body. If you specify the `runDate` field, the scheduced payment run is to be executed on the run date. If you specify the `targetDate` field, the payment run is executed immediately after it is created. <br>|

## Update a payment run

<a id="opIdPUT_PaymentRun"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payment-runs/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "autoApplyCreditMemo": "true",
    "autoApplyUnappliedPayment": "true",
    "consolidatedPayment": "true",
    "processPaymentWithClosedPM": "true",
    "targetDate": "2017-10-12"
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/payment-runs/{paymentRunId}`

Updates the information about an unexecuted payment run. Only pending payment runs can be updated.

If none of the **accountId**, **batch**, **billCycleDay**, **currency**, **paymentGatewayId**, and **billingRunId** fields is specified in the request body, the corresponding payment run collects payments for all accounts.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "autoApplyCreditMemo": "true",
  "autoApplyUnappliedPayment": "true",
  "consolidatedPayment": "true",
  "processPaymentWithClosedPM": "true",
  "targetDate": "2017-10-12"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-payment-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|paymentRunId|path|string|true|The unique ID of a payment run. For example, 402890245f097f39015f0f074a2e0566.<br>|
|body|body|[PUTPaymentRunRequest](#schemaputpaymentrunrequest)|true|none|
|» accountId|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of the customer account associated with the payment run.<br><br>This field conflicts with each of the `batch`, `billCycleDay`, `currency`, `paymentGatewayId`, and `billingRunId` fields. If there are such conflicts, an error occurs and an error message is returned.<br>|
|» applyCreditBalance|body|boolean|false|**Note:** This field is only available if you have the Credit Balance feature enabled and the Invoice Settlement feature disabled.<br><br>Whether to apply credit balances in the payment run. This field is only available when you have Invoice Settlement feature disabled.<br>|
|» autoApplyCreditMemo|body|boolean|false|**Note:** This field is only available if you have [Invoice Settlement](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement) enabled. The Invoice Settlement feature is generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 296 (March 2021). This feature includes Unapplied Payments, Credit and Debit Memo, and Invoice Item Settlement. If you want to enable Invoice Settlement, see [Invoice Settlement Enablement and Checklist Guide](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement/Invoice_Settlement_Migration_Checklist_and_Guide) for more information.<br><br>Whether to automatically apply a posted credit memo to one or more receivables in the payment run.<br>|
|» autoApplyUnappliedPayment|body|boolean|false|**Note:** This field is only available if you have [Invoice Settlement](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement) enabled. The Invoice Settlement feature is generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 296 (March 2021). This feature includes Unapplied Payments, Credit and Debit Memo, and Invoice Item Settlement. If you want to enable Invoice Settlement, see [Invoice Settlement Enablement and Checklist Guide](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement/Invoice_Settlement_Migration_Checklist_and_Guide) for more information.<br><br>Whether to automatically apply unapplied payments to  one or more receivables in the payment run.<br>|
|» batch|body|string|false|The alias name given to a batch. The batch name is a string of 50 characters or less.<br><br>This field conflicts with the `accountId` field. If they are both specified in the request body, an error occurs and an error message is returned. <br>|
|» billCycleDay|body|string|false|The billing cycle day (BCD), the day of the month when a bill run generates invoices for the account. The value must be equal to or less then 31, and 31 is mean the EOM.<br><br>This field conflicts with the `accountId` field. If they are both specified in the request body, an error occurs and an error message is returned.<br>|
|» billingRunId|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of a bill run.<br><br>This field conflicts with the `accountId` field. If they are both specified in the request body, an error occurs and an error message is returned.<br>|
|» collectPayment|body|boolean|false|Whether to process electronic payments during the execution of payment runs. <br><br>If the Payment user permission "Process Electronic Payment" is disabled, this field will be ignored.<br>|
|» consolidatedPayment|body|boolean|false|**Note:** The **Process Electronic Payment** permission also needs to be allowed for a Manage Payment Runs role to work. See [Payments Roles](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/CF_Users_and_Administrators/A_Administrator_Settings/User_Roles/e_Payments_Roles) for more information. <br><br>Whether to process a single payment for all receivables that are due on an account.<br>|
|» currency|body|string|false|A currency defined in the web-based UI administrative settings.<br><br>This field conflicts with the `accountId` field. If they are both specified in the request body, an error occurs and an error message is returned.<br>|
|» paymentGatewayId|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of the gateway instance that processes the payment.<br><br>This field conflicts with the `accountId` field. If they are both specified in the request body, an error occurs and an error message is returned.<br>|
|» processPaymentWithClosedPM|body|boolean|false|**Note:** The **Process Electronic Payment** permission also needs to be allowed for a Manage Payment Runs role to work. See [Payments Roles](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/CF_Users_and_Administrators/A_Administrator_Settings/User_Roles/e_Payments_Roles) for more information. <br><br>Whether to process payments even if the default payment method is closed.<br>|
|» runDate|body|string(date-time)|false|The date and time when the scheduled payment run is to be executed, in `yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss` format. The backend will ignore mintues and seconds in the field value. For example, if you specify `2017-03-01 11:30:37` for this value, this payment run will be run at 2017-03-01 11:00:00.<br>|
|» targetDate|body|string(date)|false|The target date used to determine which receivables to be paid in the payment run. The payments are collected for all receivables with the due date no later than the target date.<br>|

> Example responses

<h1 id="api-reference-billing-payments">Payments</h1>

## CRUD: Create a payment

<a id="opIdObject_POSTPayment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/object/payment \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "AccountId": "2c93808457d787030157e03190e748ea",
    "Amount": 2,
    "AppliedCreditBalanceAmount": 0,
    "AppliedInvoiceAmount": 2,
    "EffectiveDate": "2016-10-20",
    "InvoiceId": "2c93808457d787030157e03195604902",
    "PaymentMethodId": "2c93808457d787030157e03196d1490e",
    "Status": "Processed",
    "Type": "Electronic"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/object/payment`

Creates a payment for one or multiple invoices.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "AccountId": "2c93808457d787030157e03190e748ea",
  "Amount": 2,
  "AppliedCreditBalanceAmount": 0,
  "AppliedInvoiceAmount": 2,
  "EffectiveDate": "2016-10-20",
  "InvoiceId": "2c93808457d787030157e03195604902",
  "PaymentMethodId": "2c93808457d787030157e03196d1490e",
  "Status": "Processed",
  "Type": "Electronic"
}
```

<h3 id="crud-create-a-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|rejectUnknownFields|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether the call fails if the request body contains unknown fields.<br>With `rejectUnknownFields` set to `true`, Zuora returns a 400 response if<br>the request body contains unknown fields. The body of the 400 response is:<br><br>```json<br>{<br>    "message": "Error - unrecognised fields"<br>}<br>```<br><br>By default, Zuora ignores unknown fields in the request body.<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|body|body|[ProxyCreatePayment](#schemaproxycreatepayment)|true|none|
|» AccountId|body|string|true|The unique account ID for the customer that the payment is for.<br>|
|» AccountingCode|body|string|false|The accounting code for the payment. Accounting codes group transactions that contain similar accounting attributes.<br>|
|» Amount|body|number(double)|false|The amount of the payment.<br><br>If Invoice Settlement is enabled, this field is required.<br>|
|» AppliedCreditBalanceAmount|body|number(double)|false|If you have the Invoice Settlement feature disabled, the value of this field is the amount of the payment to apply to a credit balance. This field is only required if the `AppliedInvoiceAmount` field value is null.<br><br>If you have the Invoice Settlement feature enabled, the value of this field is created as the unapplied amount.<br>|
|» AppliedInvoiceAmount|body|number(decimal)|false|The amount of the payment to apply to an invoice. This field is only required if either the `InvoiceId` or `InvoiceNumber` field is not null.<br>|
|» AuthTransactionId|body|string|false|The authorization transaction ID from the payment gateway. Use this field for electronic payments, such as credit cards.<br>|
|» Comment|body|string|false|Additional information related to the payment.<br>|
|» EffectiveDate|body|string(date)|true|The date when the payment takes effect.<br>|
|» Gateway|body|string|false|The name of the gateway instance that processes the payment. When creating a payment, the value of this field must be a valid gateway instance name, and this gateway must support the specific payment method. If no value is specified, the default gateway on the Account will be used.<br>|
|» GatewayOptionData|body|object|false|A field used to pass gateway options. Zuora allows you to pass in special gateway-specific parameters for payments that go through the Adyen, Autorize.et, CyberSource, Merchant eSolutions, Orbital (Chase Paymentech), QValent, Vantiv, and Verifi gateways.<br><br>For each of these special parameters, you supply the name-value pair and Zuora passes it to the gateway. This allows you to add functionality that's supported by a specific gateway but currently not supported by Zuora.<br>|
|» » GatewayOption|body|[[GatewayOption](#schemagatewayoption)]|true|none|
|» GatewayOrderId|body|string|false|A merchant-specified natural key value that can be passed to the electronic payment gateway when a payment is created. If not specified, the payment number will be passed in instead.<br><br>Gateways check duplicates on the gateway order ID to ensure that the merchant do not accidentally enter the same transaction twice. This ID can also be used to do reconciliation and tie the payment to a natural key in external systems. The source of this ID varies by merchant. Some merchants use their shopping cart order IDs, and others use something different. Merchants use this ID to track transactions in their eCommerce systems.<br>|
|» GatewayResponse|body|string|false|The message returned from the payment gateway for the payment. This message is gateway-dependent.<br>|
|» GatewayResponseCode|body|string|false|The code returned from the payment gateway for the payment. This code is gateway-dependent.<br>|
|» GatewayState|body|string|false|The status of the payment in the gateway; use for reconciliation.<br>|
|» InvoiceId|body|string|false|The ID of the invoice that the payment is applied to. When applying a payment to a single invoice, this field is only required if the `InvoiceNumber` field is null.<br>|
|» InvoiceNumber|body|string|false|The unique identification number for the invoice that the payment is applied to. When applying a payment to a single invoice, this field is only required if the `InvoiceId` field is null.<br>|
|» InvoicePaymentData|body|object|false|Container for the invoice payment data. This field is only required if you apply a payment to multiple invoices.<br>|
|» » InvoicePayment|body|[[InvoicePayment](#schemainvoicepayment)]|true|none|
|» PaymentMethodId|body|string|true|The ID of the payment method used for the payment. <br>|
|» PaymentNumber|body|string|false|The unique identification number of the payment. For example, P-00000028.<br>|
|» ReferenceId|body|string|false|The transaction ID returned by the payment gateway. Use this field to reconcile payments between your gateway and Zuora Payments.<br>|
|» SoftDescriptor|body|string|false|A payment gateway-specific field that maps to Zuora for the gateways, Orbital, Vantiv and Verifi. <br><br>Zuora passes this field to Verifi directly without verification. In general, this field will be defaulted by the gateway. For Orbital, this field contains two fields separated by an asterisk, `SDMerchantName` and `SDProductionInfo`. For more information, contact your payment gateway.<br>|
|» SoftDescriptorPhone|body|string|false|A payment gateway-specific field that maps to Zuora for the gateways, Orbital, Vantiv and Verifi.<br><br>Verifi and Orbital determine how to format this string. For more information, contact your payment gateway.<br>|
|» Status|body|string|true|The status of the payment in Zuora. The value depends on the type of payments.<br><br>- If you have the Invoice Settlement feature disabled, for electronic payments, the status can be `Processed`, `Processing`, `Error`, or `Voided`. For external payments, the status can be `Processed` or `Canceled`.<br>- If you have the Invoice Settlement feature enabled, for electronic payments, the status can be `Processed`, `Processing`, `Error`, or `Canceled`. For external payments, the status can be `Processed` or `Canceled`.<br>|
|» Type|body|string|true|The type of the payment, whether the payment is external or electronic.<br>|
|» IntegrationId__NS|body|string|false|ID of the corresponding object in NetSuite. Only available if you have installed the [Zuora Connector for NetSuite](https://www.zuora.com/connect/app/?appId=265).<br>|
|» IntegrationStatus__NS|body|string|false|Status of the payment's synchronization with NetSuite. Only available if you have installed the [Zuora Connector for NetSuite](https://www.zuora.com/connect/app/?appId=265).<br>|
|» Origin__NS|body|string|false|Origin of the corresponding object in NetSuite. Only available if you have installed the [Zuora Connector for NetSuite](https://www.zuora.com/connect/app/?appId=265).<br>|
|» SyncDate__NS|body|string|false|Date when the payment was synchronized with NetSuite. Only available if you have installed the [Zuora Connector for NetSuite](https://www.zuora.com/connect/app/?appId=265).<br>|
|» Transaction__NS|body|string|false|Related transaction in NetSuite. Only available if you have installed the [Zuora Connector for NetSuite](https://www.zuora.com/connect/app/?appId=265).<br>|
|» **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|Custom fields of the Payment object. The name of each custom field has the form <code>*customField*__c</code>. Custom field names are case sensitive. See [Manage Custom Fields](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Manage_Custom_Fields) for more information.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» GatewayState|MarkedForSubmission|
|» GatewayState|Submitted|
|» GatewayState|Settled|
|» GatewayState|NotSubmitted|
|» GatewayState|FailedToSettle|
|» Status|Processed|
|» Status|Error|
|» Status|Voided|
|» Status|Canceled|
|» Type|External|
|» Type|Electronic|

```json
  "Id": "2c93808457d787030157e03197714910",

}
```

```json
    {
      "Code": "INVALID_VALUE",
      "Message": "The account number 123xProxy is invalid."
    }
  ],
  "Success": false
}
```

```json
{
  "message": "Authentication error"
}
```

## List payments

<a id="opIdGET_RetrieveAllPayments"></a>

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payments \

```

`GET /v1/payments`

**Note:** This operation is only available if you have [Invoice Settlement](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement) enabled. The Invoice Settlement feature is generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 296 (March 2021). This feature includes Unapplied Payments, Credit and Debit Memo, and Invoice Item Settlement. If you want to enable Invoice Settlement, see [Invoice Settlement Enablement and Checklist Guide](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement/Invoice_Settlement_Migration_Checklist_and_Guide) for more information. 

Retrieves the information about all payments from all your customer accounts.

### Filtering

You can use query parameters to restrict the data returned in the response. Each query parameter corresponds to one field in the response body.

If the value of a filterable field is string, you can set the corresponding query parameter to `null` when filtering. Then, you can get the response data with this field value being `null`.

Examples:

- /v1/payments?status=Processed

- /v1/payments?currency=USD&status=Processed

- /v1/payments?status=Processed&type=External&sort=+number

|---|---|---|---|---|

If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|

|accountId|query|string|false|This parameter filters the response based on the `accountId` field.<br>|
|amount|query|number(double)|false|This parameter filters the response based on the `amount` field.<br>|
|appliedAmount|query|number(double)|false|This parameter filters the response based on the `appliedAmount` field.<br>|
|createdById|query|string|false|This parameter filters the response based on the `createdById` field.<br>|

|creditBalanceAmount|query|number(double)|false|This parameter filters the response based on the `creditBalanceAmount` field.<br>|
|currency|query|string|false|This parameter filters the response based on the `currency` field.<br>|

Use a comma to separate sortable fields. For example:  *operator* *field_name*, *operator* *field_name*  <br><br>*operator* is used to mark the order of sequencing. The operator is optional. If you only specify the sortable field without any operator, the response data is sorted in descending order by this field.<br><br>  - The `-` operator indicates an ascending order.<br>  - The `+` operator indicates a descending order.<br><br>By default, the response data is displayed in descending order by payment number.<br><br>*field_name* indicates the name of a sortable field. The supported sortable fields of this operation are as below:<br><br>  - number<br>  - accountId<br>  - amount<br>  - appliedAmount<br>  - unappliedAmount<br>  - refundAmount<br>  - creditBalanceAmount<br>  - effectiveDate<br>  - createdDate<br>  - createdById<br>  - updatedDate<br>  - updatedById<br>  <br>Examples:<br><br>- /v1/payments?sort=+number<br><br>- /v1/payments?status=Processed&sort=-number,+amount<br>|

<a id="opIdPOST_CreatePayment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "accountId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d25ae90025",
    "amount": 44.1,
    "comment": "normal payment",
    "currency": "USD",
    "debitMemos": [
      {
        "amount": 4.1,
        "debitMemoId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49e6b0062",
        "items": [
          {
            "amount": 4,
            "debitMemoItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49e7a0063"
          },
          {
            "amount": 0.1,
            "taxItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49f5e0065"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "effectiveDate": "2017-03-01",
    "invoices": [
      {
        "amount": 40,
        "invoiceId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f8f10043",
        "items": [
          {
            "amount": 39,
            "invoiceItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f90c0045"
          },
          {
            "amount": 1,
            "taxItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f884003f"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "paymentMethodId": "402881e522cf4f9b0122cf5dc4020045",
    "type": "External"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/payments`

**Note:** This operation is only available if you have [Invoice Settlement](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement) enabled. The Invoice Settlement feature is generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 296 (March 2021). This feature includes Unapplied Payments, Credit and Debit Memo, and Invoice Item Settlement. If you want to enable Invoice Settlement, see [Invoice Settlement Enablement and Checklist Guide](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement/Invoice_Settlement_Migration_Checklist_and_Guide) for more information. 

Creates a payment in the following scenarios:

- A full or partial payment on an invoice or a debit memo
- A full or partial payment on several invoices and debit memos
- An unapplied payment in the following situations:
  - You do not know which customer account the payment belongs to.
  - You know which customer account the payment belongs to, but you do not know which invoice the payment is applied to.
  - You receive a payment from your customer that exceeds the balance on the invoice.
  - You receive a payment from your customer before the invoice has been created.
  - You intend to create a payment without any invoices or debit memos.
- A standalone payment. If you only need to create and process an electronic payment in Zuora through a Zuora gateway integration but settle the payment outside of Zuora, you can create a standalone payment. For a standalone payment, you can specify a currency different from the payment currency in the customer account settings. 

  The support for standalone payments is in the Early Adopter phase. If you want to use this feature, submit a request at [Zuora Global Support](http://support.zuora.com/) to enable it.

If you do not know to which customer account the payment belongs, you can create a payment without specifying a customer account.

When you create a payment, the total number of invoice items and debit memo items that the payment will apply to should be less than or equal to 10,000.

For more information, see [Create Payments](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/CB_Billing/Invoice_Settlement/A_Unapplied_Payments/Management_of_Unapplied_Payments/AA_Create_Payments) and [Create Payments Without Specifying Customer Accounts](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/CB_Billing/Invoice_Settlement/A_Unapplied_Payments/Management_of_Unapplied_Payments/AA_Create_Payments_Without_Specifying_Customer_Accounts).
    


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "accountId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d25ae90025",
  "amount": 44.1,
  "comment": "normal payment",
  "currency": "USD",
  "debitMemos": [
    {
      "amount": 4.1,
      "debitMemoId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49e6b0062",
      "items": [
        {
          "amount": 4,
          "debitMemoItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49e7a0063"
        },
        {
          "amount": 0.1,
          "taxItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49f5e0065"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "effectiveDate": "2017-03-01",
  "invoices": [
    {
      "amount": 40,
      "invoiceId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f8f10043",
      "items": [
        {
          "amount": 39,
          "invoiceItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f90c0045"
        },
        {
          "amount": 1,
          "taxItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f884003f"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "paymentMethodId": "402881e522cf4f9b0122cf5dc4020045",
  "type": "External"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|body|body|[CreatePaymentType](#schemacreatepaymenttype)|true|none|
|» accountId|body|string|false|The ID of the customer account that the payment is created for.<br>|
|» amount|body|number(double)|true|The total amount of the payment.<br>|
|» authTransactionId|body|string|false|The authorization transaction ID from the payment gateway. Use this field for electronic payments, such as credit cards.<br><br>When capturing the authorized funds after authorization enablement, `authTransactionId` must be used together with `gatewayOrderId`.<br>|
|» comment|body|string|false|Additional information related to the payment.<br>|
|» currency|body|string|true|When Standalone Payment is not enabled, the `currency` of the payment must be the same as the payment currency defined in the customer account settings through Zuora UI.<br><br>When Standalone Payment is enabled and `standalone` is `true`, the `currency` of the standalone payment can be different from the payment currency defined in the customer account settings. The amount will not be summed up to the account balance or key metrics regardless of currency.<br>|
|» debitMemos|body|[[PaymentDebitMemoApplicationCreateRequestType](#schemapaymentdebitmemoapplicationcreaterequesttype)]|false|Container for debit memos. The maximum number of debit memos is 1,000.<br>|
|» effectiveDate|body|string(date)|false|The date when the payment takes effect, in `yyyy-mm-dd` format.<br>|
|» financeInformation|body|object|false|Container for the finance information related to the payment.<br>|
|» » bankAccountAccountingCode|body|string|false|The accounting code that maps to a bank account in your accounting system.<br>|
|» » transferredToAccounting|body|string|false|Whether the payment was transferred to an external accounting system. Use this field for integration with accounting systems, such as NetSuite. <br>|
|» » unappliedPaymentAccountingCode|body|string|false|The accounting code for the unapplied payment.<br>|
|» gatewayId|body|string|false|The ID of the gateway instance that processes the payment. The ID must be a valid gateway instance ID and this gateway must support the specific payment method. <br><br>- When creating electronic payments, this field is required. <br>- When creating external payments, this field is optional.<br>|
|» gatewayOptions|body|object|false|The field used to pass gateway-specific parameters and parameter values.<br>|
|» » key|body|string|false|The name of a gateway-specific parameter.<br>|
|» » value|body|string|false|The value of the gateway-specific parameter.<br>|
|» gatewayOrderId|body|string|false|A merchant-specified natural key value that can be passed to the electronic payment gateway when a payment is created. If not specified, the payment number will be passed in instead.<br><br>Gateways check duplicates on the gateway order ID to ensure that the merchant do not accidentally enter the same transaction twice. This ID can also be used to do reconciliation and tie the payment to a natural key in external systems. The source of this ID varies by merchant. Some merchants use their shopping cart order IDs, and others use something different. Merchants use this ID to track transactions in their eCommerce systems.<br><br>When capturing the authorized funds after authorization enablement, `gatewayOrderId` must be used together with `authTransactionId`.<br>|
|» invoices|body|[[PaymentInvoiceApplicationCreateRequestType](#schemapaymentinvoiceapplicationcreaterequesttype)]|false|Container for invoices. The maximum number of invoices is 1,000.<br>|
|» mitTransactionSource|body|string|false|Payment transaction source used to differentiate the transaction source in Stored Credential Transaction framework.<br>  - `C_Unscheduled`: Cardholder-initiated transaction (CIT) that does not occur on scheduled or regularly occurring dates.<br>  - `M_Recurring`: Merchant-initiated transaction (MIT) that occurs at regular intervals.<br>  - `M_Unscheduled`: Merchant-initiated transaction (MIT) that does not occur on scheduled or regularly occurring dates.<br>|
|» paymentMethodId|body|string|false|The unique ID of the payment method that the customer used to make the payment. <br><br>If no payment method ID is specified in the request body, the default payment method for the customer account is used automatically. If the default payment method is different from the type of payments that you want to create, an error occurs.<br>|
|» referenceId|body|string|false|The transaction ID returned by the payment gateway. Use this field to reconcile payments between your gateway and Zuora Payments.<br>|
|» softDescriptor|body|string|false|A payment gateway-specific field that maps to Zuora for the gateways, Orbital, Vantiv and Verifi.|
|» softDescriptorPhone|body|string|false|A payment gateway-specific field that maps to Zuora for the gateways, Orbital, Vantiv and Verifi.|
|» standalone|body|boolean|false|This field is only available if support for standalone payments is enabled.<br><br>Specify `true` to create a standalone payment that will be processed in Zuora through Zuora gateway integration but will be settled outside of Zuora.<br><br>When `standalone` is set to `true`:<br>  - `accountId`, `amount`, `currency`, and `type` are required. <br>  - `type` must be `Electronic`.<br>  - `currency` of the payment can be different from the payment currency in the customer account settings.<br>  - The amount will not be summed up into the account balance and key metrics regardless of the payment currency.<br>  - No settlement data will be created.<br>  - Either the applied amount or the unapplied amount of the payment is zero.<br>  - The standalone payment cannot be applied, unapplied, or transferred.<br><br>Specify `false` to create an ordinary payment that will be created, processed, and settled in Zuora. The `currency` of an ordinary payment must be the same as the currency in the customer account settings.<br>|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of the payment.<br>|
|» IntegrationId__NS|body|string|false|ID of the corresponding object in NetSuite. Only available if you have installed the [Zuora Connector for NetSuite](https://www.zuora.com/connect/app/?appId=265).<br>|
|» IntegrationStatus__NS|body|string|false|Status of the payment's synchronization with NetSuite. Only available if you have installed the [Zuora Connector for NetSuite](https://www.zuora.com/connect/app/?appId=265).<br>|
|» Origin__NS|body|string|false|Origin of the corresponding object in NetSuite. Only available if you have installed the [Zuora Connector for NetSuite](https://www.zuora.com/connect/app/?appId=265).<br>|
|» SyncDate__NS|body|string|false|Date when the payment was synchronized with NetSuite. Only available if you have installed the [Zuora Connector for NetSuite](https://www.zuora.com/connect/app/?appId=265).<br>|
|» Transaction__NS|body|string|false|Related transaction in NetSuite. Only available if you have installed the [Zuora Connector for NetSuite](https://www.zuora.com/connect/app/?appId=265).<br>|
|» **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|Custom fields of the Payment object. The name of each custom field has the form <code>*customField*__c</code>. Custom field names are case sensitive. See [Manage Custom Fields](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Manage_Custom_Fields) for more information.<br>|

## Retrieve a payment

<a id="opIdGET_Payment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payments/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}`

**Note:** This operation is only available if you have [Invoice Settlement](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement) enabled. The Invoice Settlement feature is generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 296 (March 2021). This feature includes Unapplied Payments, Credit and Debit Memo, and Invoice Item Settlement. If you want to enable Invoice Settlement, see [Invoice Settlement Enablement and Checklist Guide](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement/Invoice_Settlement_Migration_Checklist_and_Guide) for more information. 

Retrieves the information about one specific payment.


<h3 id="retrieve-a-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|

If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|paymentId|path|string|true|The unique ID of a payment. For example, 8a8082e65b27f6c3015b89e4344c16b1.<br>|

## Update a payment

<a id="opIdPUT_UpdatePayment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payments/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "comment": "new comment",
    "financeInformation": {
      "transferredToAccounting": "No"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/payments/{paymentId}`

**Note:** This operation is only available if you have [Invoice Settlement](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement) enabled. The Invoice Settlement feature is generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 296 (March 2021). This feature includes Unapplied Payments, Credit and Debit Memo, and Invoice Item Settlement. If you want to enable Invoice Settlement, see [Invoice Settlement Enablement and Checklist Guide](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement/Invoice_Settlement_Migration_Checklist_and_Guide) for more information. 

Updates a payment.


> Body parameter

```json

  "comment": "new comment",
  "financeInformation": {
    "transferredToAccounting": "No"
  }
}
```

## Apply a payment

<a id="opIdPUT_ApplyPayment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payments/string/apply \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "debitMemos": [
      {
        "amount": 1.02,
        "debitMemoId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49e6b0062",
        "items": [
          {
            "amount": 1,
            "debitMemoItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49e7a0063"
          },
          {
            "amount": 0.02,
            "taxItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49f5e0065"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "effectiveDate": "2017-03-01",
    "invoices": [
      {
        "amount": 10.1,
        "invoiceId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f8f10043",
        "items": [
          {
            "amount": 10,
            "invoiceItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f90c0045"
          },
          {
            "amount": 0.1,
            "taxItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f884003f"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/payments/{paymentId}/apply`

**Note:** This operation is only available if you have [Invoice Settlement](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement) enabled. The Invoice Settlement feature is generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 296 (March 2021). This feature includes Unapplied Payments, Credit and Debit Memo, and Invoice Item Settlement. If you want to enable Invoice Settlement, see [Invoice Settlement Enablement and Checklist Guide](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement/Invoice_Settlement_Migration_Checklist_and_Guide) for more information. 

Applies an unapplied payment to invoices and debit memos.

When you apply a payment, the total number of invoice items and debit memo items that the payment will apply to must be less than or equal to 10,000.
        
If the limit is hit, you can follow the instructions:
- If you want to apply one payment to multiple invoices or debit memos, decrease the number of invoices or debit memos in the request.
- If you want to apply one payment to a single invoice or debit memo with a large volume of items, you have to specify invoice items in the request. The maximum number of invoice items that you can specify in the request is 1,000.

For more information, see [Apply Unapplied Payments to Invoices and Debit Memos](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/CB_Billing/Invoice_Settlement/A_Unapplied_Payments/Management_of_Unapplied_Payments/Apply_Unapplied_Payments_to_Invoices_and_Debit_Memos).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "debitMemos": [
    {
      "amount": 1.02,
      "debitMemoId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49e6b0062",
      "items": [
        {
          "amount": 1,
          "debitMemoItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49e7a0063"
        },
        {
          "amount": 0.02,
          "taxItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49f5e0065"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "effectiveDate": "2017-03-01",
  "invoices": [
    {
      "amount": 10.1,
      "invoiceId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f8f10043",
      "items": [
        {
          "amount": 10,
          "invoiceItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f90c0045"
        },
        {
          "amount": 0.1,
          "taxItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f884003f"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="apply-a-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|paymentId|path|string|true|The unique ID of an unapplied payment. For example, 8a8082e65b27f6c3015b89e4344c16b1.<br>|
|body|body|[ApplyPaymentType](#schemaapplypaymenttype)|true|none|
|» debitMemos|body|[[PaymentDebitMemoApplicationApplyRequestType](#schemapaymentdebitmemoapplicationapplyrequesttype)]|false|Container for debit memos. The maximum number of debit memos is 1,000.<br>|
|» effectiveDate|body|string(date)|false|The date when the payment application takes effect, in `yyyy-mm-dd` format.<br>|
|» invoices|body|[[PaymentInvoiceApplicationApplyRequestType](#schemapaymentinvoiceapplicationapplyrequesttype)]|false|Container for invoices. The maximum number of invoices is 1,000.<br>|

## Refund a payment

<a id="opIdPOST_RefundPayment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payments/string/refunds \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "comment": "Create a refund for unapplied payment.",
    "gatewayOptions": {
      "Comments": "test",
      "IPAddress": "192.168.1.1"
    },
    "methodType": "CreditCard",
    "reasonCode": "Standard Refund",
    "refundDate": "2017-03-01",
    "totalAmount": 4,
    "type": "External"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/payments/{paymentId}/refunds`

**Note:** This operation is only available if you have [Invoice Settlement](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement) enabled. The Invoice Settlement feature is generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 296 (March 2021). This feature includes Unapplied Payments, Credit and Debit Memo, and Invoice Item Settlement. If you want to enable Invoice Settlement, see [Invoice Settlement Enablement and Checklist Guide](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement/Invoice_Settlement_Migration_Checklist_and_Guide) for more information. 

Refunds a full or partial unapplied payment to your customers. To refund applied payments, you must unapply the applied payments from the invoices or debit memos, and then refund the unapplied payments to customers.

For more information, see [Refund Payments](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/CB_Billing/Invoice_Settlement/A_Unapplied_Payments/Management_of_Unapplied_Payments/Z_Refund_Payments).

For a use case of this operation, see [Refund processing](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-guides/#Refund-processing).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comment": "Create a refund for unapplied payment.",
  "gatewayOptions": {
    "Comments": "test",
    "IPAddress": "192.168.1.1"
  },
  "methodType": "CreditCard",
  "reasonCode": "Standard Refund",
  "refundDate": "2017-03-01",
  "totalAmount": 4,
  "type": "External"
}
```

<h3 id="refund-a-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|paymentId|path|string|true|The unique ID of an unapplied payment. For example, 8a8082e65b27f6c3015b89e4344c16b1.<br>|
|body|body|[PostRefundType](#schemapostrefundtype)|true|none|
|» comment|body|string|false|Comments about the refund.<br>|
|» financeInformation|body|object|false|Container for the finance information related to the refund.<br>|
|» » bankAccountAccountingCode|body|string|false|The accounting code that maps to a bank account in your accounting system.<br>|
|» » transferredToAccounting|body|string|false|Whether the refund was transferred to an external accounting system. Use this field for integration with accounting systems, such as NetSuite. <br>|
|» » unappliedPaymentAccountingCode|body|string|false|The accounting code for the unapplied payment.<br>|
|» gatewayOptions|body|object|false|The field used to pass gateway-specific parameters and parameter values.<br>|
|» » key|body|string|false|The name of a gateway-specific parameter.<br>|
|» » value|body|string|false|The value of the gateway-specific parameter.<br>|
|» methodType|body|string|false|How an external refund was issued to a customer. This field is required for an external refund and must be left empty for an electronic refund. You can issue an external refund on an electronic payment.<br>|
|» reasonCode|body|string|false|A code identifying the reason for the transaction. The value must be an existing reason code or empty. If you do not specify a value, Zuora uses the default reason code.<br>|
|» referenceId|body|string|false|The transaction ID returned by the payment gateway for an electronic refund. Use this field to reconcile refunds between your gateway and Zuora Payments.<br>|
|» refundDate|body|string(date)|false|The date when the refund takes effect, in `yyyy-mm-dd` format. The date of the refund cannot be before the payment date. Specify this field only for external refunds. Zuora automatically generates this field for electronic refunds.<br>|
|» secondRefundReferenceId|body|string|false|The transaction ID returned by the payment gateway if there is an additional transaction for the refund. Use this field to reconcile payments between your gateway and Zuora Payments.<br>|
|» softDescriptor|body|string|false|A payment gateway-specific field that maps to Zuora for the gateways, Orbital, Vantiv and Verifi.|
|» softDescriptorPhone|body|string|false|A payment gateway-specific field that maps to Zuora for the gateways, Orbital, Vantiv and Verifi.|
|» totalAmount|body|number(double)|true|The total amount of the refund. The amount cannot exceed the unapplied amount of the associated payment. If the original payment was applied to one or more invoices or debit memos, you have to unapply a full or partial payment from the invoices or debit memos, and then refund the full or partial unapplied payment to your customers. <br>|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of the refund.<br>|
|» IntegrationId__NS|body|string|false|ID of the corresponding object in NetSuite. Only available if you have installed the [Zuora Connector for NetSuite](https://www.zuora.com/connect/app/?appId=265).<br>|
|» IntegrationStatus__NS|body|string|false|Status of the refund's synchronization with NetSuite. Only available if you have installed the [Zuora Connector for NetSuite](https://www.zuora.com/connect/app/?appId=265).<br>|
|» Origin__NS|body|string|false|Origin of the corresponding object in NetSuite. Only available if you have installed the [Zuora Connector for NetSuite](https://www.zuora.com/connect/app/?appId=265).<br>|
|» SyncDate__NS|body|string|false|Date when the refund was synchronized with NetSuite. Only available if you have installed the [Zuora Connector for NetSuite](https://www.zuora.com/connect/app/?appId=265).<br>|
|» SynctoNetSuite__NS|body|string|false|Specifies whether the refund should be synchronized with NetSuite. Only available if you have installed the [Zuora Connector for NetSuite](https://www.zuora.com/connect/app/?appId=265).<br>|
|» **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|Custom fields of the Refund object. The name of each custom field has the form <code>*customField*__c</code>. Custom field names are case sensitive. See [Manage Custom Fields](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Manage_Custom_Fields) for more information.<br>|

## Unapply a payment

<a id="opIdPUT_UnapplyPayment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/payments/string/unapply \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "debitMemos": [
      {
        "amount": 1.02,
        "debitMemoId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49e6b0062",
        "items": [
          {
            "amount": 1,
            "debitMemoItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49e7a0063"
          },
          {
            "amount": 0.02,
            "taxItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49f5e0065"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "effectiveDate": "2017-03-01",
    "invoices": [
      {
        "amount": 10.1,
        "invoiceId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f8f10043",
        "items": [
          {
            "amount": 10,
            "invoiceItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f90c0045"
          },
          {
            "amount": 0.1,
            "taxItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f884003f"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/payments/{paymentId}/unapply`

**Note:** This operation is only available if you have [Invoice Settlement](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement) enabled. The Invoice Settlement feature is generally available as of Zuora Billing Release 296 (March 2021). This feature includes Unapplied Payments, Credit and Debit Memo, and Invoice Item Settlement. If you want to enable Invoice Settlement, see [Invoice Settlement Enablement and Checklist Guide](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/Billing/Billing_and_Payments/Invoice_Settlement/Invoice_Settlement_Migration_Checklist_and_Guide) for more information. 

Unapplies an applied payment from invoices and debit memos.

When you unapply a payment, the total number of invoice items and debit memo items that the payment will unapply from must be less than or equal to 10,000.

If the limit is hit, you can follow the instructions:
- If you want to unapply one payment without specifying invoices or debit memos, you have to specify the invoices or debit memos in the request.
- If you want to unapply one payment from multiple specified invoices or debit memos, decrease the number of invoices or debit memos in the request.
- If you want to unapply one payment from a single invoice or debit memo with a large volume of items, you have to specify invoice items in the request. The maximum number of invoice items that you can specify in the request is 1,000.

For more information, see [Unapply Payments from Invoices and Debit Memos](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/CB_Billing/Invoice_Settlement/A_Unapplied_Payments/Management_of_Unapplied_Payments/Unapply_Payments_from_Invoices_and_Debit_Memos).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "debitMemos": [
    {
      "amount": 1.02,
      "debitMemoId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49e6b0062",
      "items": [
        {
          "amount": 1,
          "debitMemoItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49e7a0063"
        },
        {
          "amount": 0.02,
          "taxItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87e49f5e0065"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "effectiveDate": "2017-03-01",
  "invoices": [
    {
      "amount": 10.1,
      "invoiceId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f8f10043",
      "items": [
        {
          "amount": 10,
          "invoiceItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f90c0045"
        },
        {
          "amount": 0.1,
          "taxItemId": "4028905f5a87c0ff015a87d3f884003f"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="unapply-a-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Zuora-Track-Id|header|string|false|A custom identifier for tracing the API call. If you set a value for this header, Zuora returns the same value in the response headers. This header enables you to associate your system process identifiers with Zuora API calls, to assist with troubleshooting in the event of an issue.<br><br>The value of this field must use the US-ASCII character set and must not include any of the following characters: colon (`:`), semicolon (`;`), double quote (`"`), and quote (`'`).<br>|
|Zuora-Entity-Ids|header|string|false|An entity ID. If you have [Zuora Multi-entity](https://knowledgecenter.zuora.com/BB_Introducing_Z_Business/Multi-entity) enabled and the OAuth token is valid for more than one entity, you must use this header to specify which entity to perform the operation in. If the OAuth token is only valid for a single entity, or you do not have Zuora Multi-entity enabled, you do not need to set this header.<br>|
|paymentId|path|string|true|The unique ID of an applied payment. For example, 8a8082e65b27f6c3015b89e4344c16b1.<br>|
|body|body|[UnapplyPaymentType](#schemaunapplypaymenttype)|true|none|
|» debitMemos|body|[[PaymentDebitMemoApplicationUnapplyRequestType](#schemapaymentdebitmemoapplicationunapplyrequesttype)]|false|Container for debit memos. The maximum number of debit memos is 1,000.<br>|
|» effectiveDate|body|string(date)|false|The date when the payment is unapplied, in `yyyy-mm-dd` format.<br>|
|» invoices|body|[[PaymentInvoiceApplicationUnapplyRequestType](#schemapaymentinvoiceapplicationunapplyrequesttype)]|false|Container for invoices. The maximum number of invoice is 1,000.<br>|

## CRUD: Update a product rate plan charge tier

<a id="opIdObject_PUTProductRatePlanChargeTier"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v1/object/product-rate-plan-charge-tier/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "Price": 1.99
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/object/product-rate-plan-charge-tier/{id}`

Updates the price of a product rate plan charge tier.

To make other updates to product rate plan charge tiers, use [CRUD: Update a product rate plan charge](https://www.zuora.com/developer/api-reference/#operation/Object_PUTProductRatePlanCharge) and specify `ProductRatePlanChargeTierData` in the request body.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "Price": 1.99
}
```
